The live comparisons still exercise the legacy rejection that spends the registry state output. The ruled rejection reads that output by reference and never spends it. Agreement with the legacy path is not acceptance of the ruled design. The earlier processing-window consumer requirement and the unresolved refund-routing requirement remain open. Historical results below retain their original revision and evidence binding; they do not establish current acceptance.

consumer-conformance-record.name: docs-consumer-conformance/consumer-conformance-record-02
consumer-conformance-record.text: As a Singular integrator, I can replay the current conformance interface, distinguish partial evidence from completed coverage, and trace older observations to the candidate that produced them. The connected naming release journey is documented separately in recovery and permanent retirement.

current-registry-mode-integration.name: docs-consumer-conformance/current-registry-mode-integration-01
current-registry-mode-integration.text: The released interface follows the six-field registry-mode state contract above. The historical reports below retain their original transaction identities, measurements and limitations; they are not current execution claims. Coverage requires fresh receipts bound to the source and blueprint being replayed. A build or a green check of expected debt grants no coverage.

current-replay-commands.name: docs-consumer-conformance/current-replay-commands-01
current-replay-commands.text: Run from the repository or extracted source root with Nix available. Use a fresh directory outside the tracked tree for each family. The generic session runs ten rows and may also emit its execution-units-and-transaction-size measurement receipt; the serialization session runs five devnet rows and two local checks. Superseded rows remain listed and are not runtime commands.

current-replay-commands.name: docs-consumer-conformance/current-replay-commands-02
current-replay-commands.text: These are expected result contracts, not claims that an arbitrary nonzero exit is acceptable. Check the terminal row counts, exact receipt IDs, source/blueprint binding, per-row verdicts and named residuals. A crash, missing receipt or failed control fails the replay. The CI workflow checks those details against the actual output; partial and held rows remain debt even when that regression check is green.

current-replay-commands.name: docs-consumer-conformance/current-replay-commands-03
current-replay-commands.text: Armed controls use a separate fresh receipt directory. Their nonzero exit must name the intended failed assertion: the wrong refusal reason, forged value or datum, weak authenticator, corrupted state derivation (legacy flag unapplied-address), wrong constructor index, wrong parameter count or deliberately missing witness. The normal partial exit alone does not prove an armed control fired. See conformance.yml for the executable session and receipt checks.

current-replay-commands.name: docs-consumer-conformance/current-replay-commands-04
current-replay-commands.text: The Fork oracle and its probes remain available without a node or blueprint; their output is local proof evidence, not proof-step-constructor-witnesses completion:

current-replay-commands.name: docs-consumer-conformance/current-replay-commands-05
current-replay-commands.text: The runner gives each node a unique temporary directory. Receipts are written under the selected output directory and are never inherited as current merely because an older run succeeded.

historical-execution-reports.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-execution-reports-01
historical-execution-reports.text: Historical scope: every report from here through “Historical limits” describes the earlier source revisions named in its provenance. Present-tense wording in those retained reports belongs to those revisions. The current contract above supersedes their owner fields, state arity, accepting-path expectations and pending-E17 descriptions. Do not use their measurements or receipts as evidence for the current candidate.

historical-execution-reports.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-execution-reports-02
historical-execution-reports.text: Devnet sessions run in order, each on an isolated node with its own published world: the generic registry rows first — the four issue-#63 rows plus the issue-#70 rows below — then the canonical identity rows, then the serialization boundary rows. Two further checks, blueprint-encoding-round-trip and script-parameter-application, never start a node at all: they compare Haskell values against the compiled blueprint read at run time, so a reader totalling "rows executed on a real devnet" counts the thirteen generic, five canonical-identity and five serialization rows below — never the local checks. The counts are kept visibly separate for exactly that reason.

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-01
historical-limits.text: Programs with end-to-end references: insert-key, retract-inside-window and reject-after-window run as programs in the registry session, their state computed from those receipts; the epic-16 CageSpec examples they cite remain supporting references. historical-owner-signed-sweep and historical-registry-termination cite none: the examples they cited were removed on 2026-09-12 (f3a68b1b), nothing runs either row, and both are superseded by the ownerless-registry ruling (no sweep, no termination) — history earns no conformance credit.

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-02
historical-limits.text: Executed, unmet by ruling, not a pass: reject-before-deadline-consumer-requirement records the early rejection the consumer forbids and the chain accepts, kept unmet by operator ruling 2026-10-01 (unmet-by-ruling). fold-against-superseded-root, surplus-fold-actions and wrong-redeemer-constructor-index: the chain refuses, Lean has no counterpart to compare with, kept unmet by operator ruling 2026-10-02 ("Narrow #287") (lambdasistemi/singular#346, lambdasistemi/singular#345, lambdasistemi/singular#347).

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-03
historical-limits.text: Executed holds, not passes: empty-fold and request-value-and-refund-routing remain held by execution. empty-fold records the pre-revision empty-fold conflict with R8_empty_fold_refused; request-value-and-refund-routing violates the consumer's required operation-specific fold value routing (Registry.processBody, Registry.stepFn, Cage.delegated_is_registry). R11_contribute_value states the deposit amount and is not that fold requirement. Upstream #100/#101 are referenced proposals, not a delivered partition fix: #101 is open, and Singular owns the required local repair. R5_plugin_pinned concerns the plugin, not a registry owner. The consumer requirements stay unmet; a held row is never a pass, and the verdicts move only by execution. historical-owner-change's owner change is retained as defect evidence of the outstanding owner gate, resolved-by-ruling, with its defect owned by epic 17.

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-04
historical-limits.text: Superseded, never pending: historical-owner-signed-sweep, historical-non-owner-sweep and historical-registry-termination asserted registry-owner authority, a sweep or a termination that does not exist — observations preserved, claims withdrawn, no execution credit for changed applicability. retired-stake-hook-with-withdrawal/retired-stake-hook-without-withdrawal are retired: the registry interface has no stake_script hook, so nothing runs them.

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-05
historical-limits.text: Uncovered: proof-step-constructor-witnesses, the five consumer-resolution requirements and fold-batch-size-boundary–observed-toolchain-and-environment print uncovered (as do retired-stake-hook-with-withdrawal/retired-stake-hook-without-withdrawal, retired, and historical-owner-signed-sweep/historical-registry-termination, superseded — no receipts). proof-step-constructor-witnesses is not merely uncovered: its Fork finding is filed for a user story and the row stays unmarked until that story resolves — an unmarked row with a finding, never a gap and never a pass. request-and-mint-constructor-witnesses's Migrating gap is of the recorded kind, with its validator-read reason beside the receipts.

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-06
historical-limits.text: Schema pending (epic 17): blueprint-encoding-round-trip, submitted-datum-byte-round-trip and state-fields-chain-round-trip describe the six-field owner-bearing OnChainTokenState. The ownerless schema repair is pending; their expectations are superseded at that repair, their receipts stay valid as history, and the rows will be re-executed with fresh receipts against the repaired blueprint — coverage is not inherited across a wire-format change. Epic 17's antecedent ownerless repair exists locally (f3a68b1) but is not accepted and not merged; nothing here cherry-picks it, and the affected runtime checks follow the definitive schema artifacts when the explicit handoff arrives — integration stays serialized behind it.

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-07
historical-limits.text: Green expected-debt CI grants no conformance credit: the workflow's generic-rows step asserts declared debt — exact receipt set, exact verdict per receipt, held set exactly empty-fold request-value-and-refund-routing, unmet set exactly reject-before-deadline-consumer-requirement fold-against-superseded-root surplus-fold-actions, nothing failing — and nothing more. It pays neither the held rows nor a full execution-units-and-transaction-size, and strict completion and release stay RED on that debt.

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-08
historical-limits.text: Out of scope: checkpoint-and-treasury-policy (cardano-keri), the naming rows (epic 16 demonstration, not consumer evidence), LR/LT rows (epic 17).

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-09
historical-limits.text: The registry-identity rows authenticate the canonical registry as the consumer derives it from the published seed. They do not evidence the serialization boundary (serialization), the constructor coverage (update-redeemer-constructor-witnesses–request-and-mint-constructor-witnesses) or the batch limits (fold-batch-size-boundary).

historical-limits.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-limits-10
historical-limits.text: The measurements above are devnet folds of single requests. They say nothing about batch limits (fold-batch-size-boundary) or any other environment (observed-toolchain-and-environment records the observed one below).

historical-observed-environment.name: docs-consumer-conformance/historical-observed-environment-01
historical-observed-environment.text: cardano-node 10.7.0, GHC 9.12.3, Aiken compiler v1.1.21 (blueprint hal/mpf 0.0.0), unapplied state script pinned d42860fa972c8a325daae773adc372795c48cf365d0a72b137c749d3 with one declared parameter, applied state script ce7615f6ba4de80dfa9b9c6aef680666472ba4ed7e640ff55aad7c6e, unapplied request script hash 8970c286… (re-pinned from 64d1afbfe585…/874e476d7408…/6b5ce7… by the issue-#79 imported-validator repair; onchain/REPAIR.patch records the change, PROVENANCE.md the authority). The issue-#70 rows were executed against blueprint state:ce7615f6ba4de80dfa9b9c6aef680666472ba4ed7e640ff55aad7c6e request:8970c286…; the pre-#79 executions (historical-permissionless-fold's refusal, the former bespoke retraction and the stale-request/proof refusals) are history at the earlier hashes. Environments other than this devnet shape are explicitly not covered.

measurements.name: docs-consumer-conformance/measurements-01
measurements.text: Ship run: base b3f4b5a, clean tree, cardano-node 10.7.0. The issue-#70 generic session's ship run: base 1d98d51, clean tree, cardano-node 10.7.0 — every generic receipt below names that base with dirty: false, and the held rows carry their acceptances with transaction ids and measurements because their controls write none.

measurements.name: docs-consumer-conformance/measurements-02
measurements.text: Serialization ship run: base b2201c3, clean tree, cardano-node 10.7.0 — every receipt below names that base with dirty: false. Each invocation observes the tree before creating its output, and ships from a fresh output directory, so no run ever measures the previous run's receipts. The defect this guards against reported dirty: true on clean trees; its direction is conservative — it can block a valid ship, it can never let a dirty tree pass as clean — and no merged receipt ever claimed clean while dirty.

measurements.name: docs-consumer-conformance/measurements-03
measurements.text: Maxima queried from the running node, never hardcoded: maxTxExUnits 140000000 mem / 10000000000 cpu, maxTxSize 16384 bytes.

measurements.name: docs-consumer-conformance/measurements-04
measurements.text: Execution units stay under 3.8% of the maxima for every row (worst: request-value-and-refund-routing's crossed-refunds fold at 3.77% cpu, still ~26× headroom; tokenless-output-authentication reports zeros honestly: no script purpose exists to evaluate). Serialized size is the tight dimension at ~71% of maxTxSize for folds and ~52% for boots; larger batches (fold-batch-size-boundary) may press against it first. The canonical session's worst case is recorded in its execution-units-and-transaction-size receipt; the registry session's execution-units-and-transaction-size reads the worst accepting folds of update-existing-key, delete-existing-key and reinsert-deleted-key off their receipts' steps, and its other rows' worst cases live in their own receipts; the serialization rows carry theirs in the row receipts, and no serialization execution-units-and-transaction-size is claimed yet. Refusal reasons keep every failing script hash in ledger order — a tampered fold can fail two scripts, and trimming volume never trims identities — under the same run-enforced 16KB bound.

model-compared-registration-and-retireme.name: docs-consumer-conformance/model-compared-registration-and-retirement-candidate-229-01
model-compared-registration-and-retireme.text: A local clean candidate at 9b42458ffc1fab6bf9b7cf88ef44884e24333b8b ran the registration and retirement chapters on a Cardano devnet. Its retained receipts carry five and seven model-and-chain step records respectively. The executable driver supplies the model outcome and all nine declared observations for each accepted step; the reader-facing book renders the story programs from those receipts. This is candidate evidence, not merge, release or independent acceptance.

model-compared-registration-and-retireme.name: docs-consumer-conformance/model-compared-registration-and-retirement-candidate-229-02
model-compared-registration-and-retireme.text: The node did not supply a Plutus trace name for the refused folds. The receipts retain the script hash and the empty trace rather than inferring a branch name. An accepting control establishes that the builder can fold a valid request in the same run.

model-compared-registration-and-retireme.name: docs-consumer-conformance/model-compared-registration-and-retirement-candidate-229-03
model-compared-registration-and-retireme.text: The former two-request batch allocation check is no longer a current conformance claim. The driver evaluates one request per transaction, so the specified per-kind-and-key batch mint rule has no executable consumer in these chapters. The old batch evidence remains historical to its own revision. The former receipt-field appendix examples were removed with their schema; new appendix checks validate the generic step records.

model-compared-registration-and-retireme.name: docs-consumer-conformance/model-compared-registration-and-retirement-candidate-229-04
model-compared-registration-and-retireme.text: The wire these rows and the archive verb speak.

model-compared-registration-and-retireme.name: docs-consumer-conformance/model-compared-registration-and-retirement-candidate-229-05
model-compared-registration-and-retireme.text: Everything on this page, and the release archive's packaged insert-active command, runs on the final request encoding: the edge index at field 3 and the deposit at field 4, as set out above.

model-compared-registration-and-retireme.name: docs-consumer-conformance/model-compared-registration-and-retirement-candidate-229-06
model-compared-registration-and-retireme.text: The re-cut carried its own enforcing check rather than being asserted. For exactly one commit the cage compiled BOTH encodings, and every other-edge fixture was folded under each of them and required to give the same verdict with the same refusal reason, receipted per fixture. The commit after it removed the old codec. That pair — the receipt at the dual-codec commit, the removal at its successor — is the evidence a one-commit rewrite cannot produce, and it is what stands behind the side-by-side table above.

permanent-contract-and-preserved-consume.name: docs-consumer-conformance/permanent-contract-and-preserved-consumer-evidence-00
permanent-contract-and-preserved-consume.text: Permanent contract and preserved consumer evidence.

permanent-contract-and-preserved-consume.name: docs-consumer-conformance/permanent-contract-and-preserved-consumer-evidence-01
permanent-contract-and-preserved-consume.text: The first milestone's fixed contract admits registration (insertActive) and permanent termination (updateTerminal). All seven edge values remain encodable in request datums and fold redeemers, but witnessTerminal, insertAbsent, updateActive, deleteAbsent and deleteActive fail at the permanent state validator, including independently constructed requests and mixed batches. Application payload updates leave the registry leaf unchanged; they are not the excluded updateActive registry transition.

permanent-contract-and-preserved-consume.name: docs-consumer-conformance/permanent-contract-and-preserved-consumer-evidence-02
permanent-contract-and-preserved-consume.text: The seven-edge interface and older receipts below describe the preserved broader consumer contract. They do not establish current permanent-contract successes. Its generic consumer expectations remain recorded, and the new permanent requirement remains uncovered without a bounded live consumer comparison receipt. The candidate evidence separates compiled refusal tests, connected CLI execution and their limits. Defined redeemers, missing CLI commands and setup failures are not evidence of behavioral refusal.

proof-step-constructor-witnesses-unmarke.name: docs-consumer-conformance/proof-step-constructor-witnesses-unmarked-and-escalated-01
proof-step-constructor-witnesses-unmarke.text: proof-step-constructor-witnesses carries no receipt and prints uncovered: Branch and Leaf are witnessed on chain across many accepted folds, but no accepted fold has ever carried a Fork, and two independently ground lone-Fork absence proofs — each verified by the mts Haskell stack against its own root — are refused by the compiled validator with a bare CekError at build-time evaluation. The full bundle (keys, trie shape, both verdicts, the refusal bytes, what could not be determined, and the bounded consumer consequence) is filed as a user story escalation; the offline oracle (find-fork-keys, check-fork-exclusion) and shape probes (show-nibbles, show-d-proof, show-all-proofs) reproduce every offline claim. This is a finding held open, not a gap and not a pass.

redeemers-that-are-gone.name: docs-consumer-conformance/redeemers-that-are-gone-01
redeemers-that-are-gone.text: The naming application's spend redeemer becomes Maintain, Retire, Recover; Fold and Cancel are removed with the pending-claim lifecycle they served. Its mint redeemer becomes the single Approve { edge, key, owner, destination }; WithdrawApproval and InsertApproval are removed. The representative policy is retired in favour of the one parametrised witness policy, instantiated three times.

registration-journeys-the-previous-desig.name: docs-consumer-conformance/registration-journeys-the-previous-design-against-the-no-pin-design-00
registration-journeys-the-previous-desig.text: Registration journeys: the previous design against the no-pin design.

registration-journeys-the-previous-desig.name: docs-consumer-conformance/registration-journeys-the-previous-design-against-the-no-pin-design-01
registration-journeys-the-previous-desig.text: As an integrator, I read what happens to a booked registration that is folded, reclaimed or cleaned up, under the previous design and under the no-pin design, and I see that these statements are published uncovered: no executable comparison with the application-held model backs them yet.

registration-journeys-the-previous-desig.name: docs-consumer-conformance/registration-journeys-the-previous-design-against-the-no-pin-design-02
registration-journeys-the-previous-desig.text: Four rows in the group registration-journeys state the outcomes. The outcomes are those the declarations OpenDatumApplicationHeld.Money.oldAllocation and OpenDatumApplicationHeld.Money.newAllocation state; the rows name the declarations and retype no number.

the-cage-datum-a-third-constructor.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-cage-datum-a-third-constructor-00
the-cage-datum-a-third-constructor.text: The cage datum: a third constructor.

the-cage-datum-a-third-constructor.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-cage-datum-a-third-constructor-01
the-cage-datum-a-third-constructor.text: The absent custody key is the identity of the output's sole non-ADA asset, which must have quantity one. It is not duplicated in the datum. The retired two-field constructor-2 wire is therefore incompatible and must not decode as AbsentCustody.

the-canonical-identity-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-canonical-identity-rows-01
the-canonical-identity-rows.text: A designation split publishes the canonical seed; canonical-seed-identity boots the canonical registry from it; rival-seed-authentication initializes a rival from a second seed through the same bootstrap path; a second split publishes the rival seed, so no boot can ever consume the wrong UTxO as its funder.

the-canonical-identity-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-canonical-identity-rows-02
the-canonical-identity-rows.text: rival-seed-authentication asserts an acceptance: the ledger takes the rival, and the consumer's authentication is what excludes it. The receipt records the ledger's verdict (accepted, with the rival's txid and measurements); the rejection is asserted on chain-read assets and named in the run — never relabelled as a refusal, never skipped because the outcome reads oddly. The acceptance is the finding, and it is the accepted design. policy-address-only-authentication-control is what makes rival-seed-authentication worth anything: a check that cannot fail proves nothing, so the weak authenticator's acceptance of the rival is itself executed and required.

the-contract-and-its-binding.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-contract-and-its-binding-01
the-contract-and-its-binding.text: The rows answer to the consumer contract source-bound to lambdasistemi/cardano-keri@14a64a4681d3e429fab5877062b5c476c2a4bfe2: the registry design rulings (eleven operator rulings and fourteen registry theorems) and docs/user/consumer-checklist.md. cardano-keri consumes the generic registry — Insert, Update, Delete — not the naming application, whose restriction refuses Delete and reuse by design. No naming evidence can establish any row here, and none is claimed.

the-contract-and-its-binding.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-contract-and-its-binding-02
the-contract-and-its-binding.text: The canonical identity rows (#69) carry the correction epic 16 executed: cardano-keri's ruling is that the registry provides identity uniqueness, but a permissionless ledger cannot prohibit a rival registry — a consistent initialization from a second seed passes every frozen check and the node accepts it (offchain/naming-correspondence.md, "What t50 settled"). Canonical identity is therefore a derivation the consumer authenticates, not a refusal the chain performs: the canonical registry token's name is SHA-256 of the canonical seed's outRef, that seed can never be spent twice, and a rival from another seed can never carry that name.

the-decided-difference.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-decided-difference-01
the-decided-difference.text: A booked registration that can never be folded, because its key is already registered or for any other reason, is not rejected early. It stays pending until its refund address reclaims it inside the reclaim window, or until anyone cleans it up after that window and the deposit returns to the refund address. Under the previous design a folder could reject such a request at once, with evidence of the mismatch, while it could still be folded or retracted. The previous design's requirements for rejection after the window, rejection before the deadline, request value and refund routing, the rejection and retraction refund controls, and rejection inside the processing and retraction windows stay published exactly as they were, with the dated qualification at the top of this page.

the-denominator.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-denominator-01
the-denominator.text: conformance/rows.json carries 55 rows, 54 owned: one permanent contract requirement, five registry identity requirements, twenty-five registry operation requirements, eight serialization requirements, five consumer resolution requirements, three execution-limit requirements, four registration journey requirements and three update and termination journey requirements (stated below), plus the checkpoint and treasury policy (bonds, poison, the juvenility window W, the signature threshold) recorded as out of scope — it belongs to cardano-keri's checkpoint machine and treasury, explicitly never claimed by Singular. list prints the owned denominator separately so the boundary stays visible. Superseded and held rows stay in the denominator and visible to completeness accounting: relabelling a row pays no coverage and shrinks no board.

the-denominator.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-denominator-02
the-denominator.text: rows.json never carries executed: the declared field is the coverage plan and the parser rejects the string. A row prints as executed only when a run receipt for it exists and matches the current base (--receipts DIR or CONFORMANCE_RECEIPTS).

the-generic-registry-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-generic-registry-rows-01
the-generic-registry-rows.text: Against a real devnet, one cage, one key, in order:

the-generic-registry-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-generic-registry-rows-02
the-generic-registry-rows.text: insert-occupied-key's refusal is a node verdict on a submitted transaction, the li-refusals bar: the fold is hand-built (the library builder cannot emit a transaction whose scripts do not evaluate) and calibrated against the library builder on every valid fold — same inputs, state output, refund destinations and Modify proofs — so the refused shape differs from a library fold only in the operation under test. The eval-time refusal the builder reports first is kept as a log line, never as the verdict. Each receipt records where its refusal was observed (venue: node-submit for every row here), and refusal reasons are trimmed to their attribution (failure class, script hash, machine error) — receipts stay under a run-enforced 16KB bound, because a receipt nobody can open is weak evidence.

the-generic-registry-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-generic-registry-rows-03
the-generic-registry-rows.text: Had the chain accepted the occupied insert, that would be a finding reported with the accepted transaction — never relabelled as a refusal.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-01
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: The table preserves the eleven requirements and their historical observations. The current generic session runs ten rows, followed by its session receipt; the retraction-window requirement now runs separately as a three-step story compared with the model. The remaining bespoke refusal rows attribute the refusal to the script that failed and retain their accepting controls.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-02
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: The retraction story gives the registry thirty seconds for processing and thirty more for retraction. Its waits follow the submission times read from the booked requests and those registry durations. The model reads the witness from each built transaction; the ledger refusal is attributed by the applied request script hash, without claiming an observable live refusal name. Open validity intervals remain a named gap: the model represents finite bounds only, while the Aiken tests establish the open-interval not-phase2 refusal.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-03
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: Four dispositions, never to be mistaken for one another.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-04
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: Unmet by ruling (unmet-by-ruling; reject-before-deadline-consumer-requirement, fold-against-superseded-root, surplus-fold-actions, wrong-redeemer-constructor-index): executed, and kept unmet by an operator ruling. The one verdict carries two meanings, and every row states which. reject-before-deadline-consumer-requirement: the registry deliberately does not do what the consumer requirement states, kept unmet by operator ruling 2026-10-01. The consumer requires that a folder must not reject a request during its processing window (cardano-keri R9_reject_needs_rejectable, 0e638fad, blob d38e81c0); Singular's model lets a folder reject a request with no timing admission, and the chain accepts that reject (#320). Alignment is cardano-keri#468. fold-against-superseded-root, surplus-fold-actions and wrong-redeemer-constructor-index: the chain refuses, Lean has no counterpart to compare with, kept unmet by operator ruling 2026-10-02 ("Narrow #287"); follow-ups: fold-against-superseded-root lambdasistemi/singular#346, surplus-fold-actions lambdasistemi/singular#345, wrong-redeemer-constructor-index lambdasistemi/singular#347. The session ends non-zero while any row is unmet; it is never a pass.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-05
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: Dated note, 2026-10-13 (decision B, ticket 494 slice three, ahead of validators 495): the dedicated in-window row is now a lawful lifecycle-mismatch rejection (a second insertActive for a key already Active, with bound mismatch evidence, both sides accepting, owner refunded) and stays green; the generic standing row now books a foldable insertActive for a fresh key with expiry evidence in-window, refused by the model for reject-not-expired and accepted by the chain (tampered refunds refused by both for different reasons), published as unmet with a tripwire for lambdasistemi/singular#495 (the validators ticket that must flip the row by refusing the untampered in-window reject). Ticket 320's early-rejection history above is not edited. Held (held-q002; empty-fold, request-value-and-refund-routing): executed, with the consumer requirements still unmet. empty-fold recorded a conflict with the pre-revision Singular model; rejecting empty batches is now approved. request-value-and-refund-routing requires the operation-specific value-routing repair. The rows move only after the required implementation and execution evidence is accepted. Resolved-by-ruling (historical-owner-change): a ruling settled the row's question; the observation is retained as defect evidence of the outstanding owner gate — never a pass, never an owner-semantics claim. Superseded (historical-owner-signed-sweep, historical-non-owner-sweep, historical-registry-termination): the expectation asserted authority, a sweep or a termination that does not exist at this commit; observations are preserved, claims are withdrawn, and no execution credit attaches. Retired (retired-stake-hook-with-withdrawal, retired-stake-hook-without-withdrawal): the registry interface has no stake_script hook, so nothing runs them.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-06
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: Evidence provenance. The receipts cited in this section are the generic session's ship run, taken fresh at clean tip 1d98d51 after the receipt-overwrite repair (blueprint state:ce7615f6… request:8970c286…, cardano-node 10.7.0, every receipt dirty: false, every held row carrying its acceptance with transaction id and measurements). historical-permissionless-fold's first post-repair execution was at clean tip 748c4a9 (txid fe54d3a6…); its ship-run repetition at 1d98d51 is 4142f7d6…. The overwritten pre-repair receipts are retained only as evidence of that defect.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-07
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: Held rows (operator question (Q-002), story 2). empty-fold and request-value-and-refund-routing are executed holds, never passes; surplus-fold-actions, held when this history was written, is now unmet by ruling (above). Only empty-fold was established as a direct conflict between the two model results. In the pinned pre-revision contract, Singular's Lean permits the empty fold (foldItems, | s, [] => .ok — Model.lean 188–189) and pairs each request with exactly one action in its FoldItem, so a surplus tail is unmodelled; State carries no owner field and Action.fold routes no refunds. Singular.Statements.fold_iff (Model.lean 250–256) makes its five conjuncts sufficient — native spend, fold items, net-mint match, representative-mint and application-mint witnesses — and no owner is among them: folding is permissionless. The consumer's theorems require the empty batch refused (R8_empty_fold_refused) and the 1:1 accounting. Its fold value routing is not R11_contribute_value — that states the deposit amount, and R11_retract_value states bond+tip on retract; fold routing lives in the consumer's Registry.processBody, Registry.stepFn and the Cage.delegated_is_registry equality, and it is operation-specific: register/revive lock the deposit into a checkpoint, goDormant/goConvicted/convict refund to the recorded owner, rejection returns the operation bond — guarded by rejectable and userPostable, not on demand — and the fold tip goes to the folder. A blanket exact-refund repair would preserve the wrong value mode and prevent checkpoint funding. Upstream #100/#101 are referenced proposals, not a delivered partition fix: #101 is open, and Singular owns the required local repair. R5_plugin_pinned needs a distinction this page previously collapsed. It is about the plugin, not a registry owner: the bound Registry.Sys carries plugin, and the consumer's fold checks pl = s.plugin. So registry-owner privileges and fields are superseded — the operator ruled Singular has no registry-owner role, and there is no owner to pin — but the application/plugin identity correspondence is not waived by that. The required application and native-witness bindings and the policy bindings remain required, and must be established through the actual ownerless representation; this is not a reason to reintroduce stake_script or to assert its old mechanism is the required one. The remaining requirements stay unmet; the receipts carry verdict held-q002 and the session ends non-zero while anything is held — a hold can never read as a pass, and a verdict moves only by execution. historical-owner-change is resolved-by-ruling, not a fourth unresolved hold: its receipt carries resolved-by-ruling, its acceptance stays defect evidence, and it is outside the held-set.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-08
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: A repair this slice had to make to keep that sentence true: a refused control used to submit through the same path as a refusal ROW and wrote its refusal under the row's id, so empty-fold/surplus-fold-actions/request-value-and-refund-routing's held receipts were being replaced by their controls' refusals in every earlier receipts directory — receipts asserting the opposite of the executed finding (historical-owner-change's survived only because its control was retired, which is what isolated the cause). The control now writes nothing: its outcome is run-log evidence under its own identity, it cannot silently pass (an accepted control fails the run as a FINDING; a refusal that does not attribute fails the run naming the mismatch), and the receipt policy is unit-tested to discriminate — a control never overwrites a held receipt, a refusal row always writes, a non-attributing refusal writes nothing. The overwritten historical receipts in /tmp/t70-receipts* are kept untouched as evidence of the defect, never relabelled as fresh proof; the receipts cited by this page are the ones taken fresh at the clean tip after the repair.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-09
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: historical-permissionless-fold and F-002, both halves by execution. An independent audit found that the runner itself always supplied the state owner's signature, so no fold row in the suite could have observed the owner gate; historical-permissionless-fold was built as the exact regression property. Executed against the pre-#79 candidate it was REFUSED, attributed to the state script, and recorded diverges-from-lean (receipt retained as history). After epic 17's #79 repair it was executed again: the fold with no owner signer is accepted (agrees-with-model, txid 4142f7d6… at the ship run, fe54d3a6… at the first post-repair execution, blueprint state:ce7615f6… request:8970c286… both times), and the same fold with the owner signer is accepted in-run. Both acceptances are the post-repair evidence, not a weakened test: the two transactions differ in the signer set alone, so the acceptance is attributable to the removed gate. The expectation was always accept; what moved is the candidate, and the verdict moved by execution only — never by editing a row or flipping a stored receipt.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-10
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: The owner-dependency extent. Before #79, every fold-based row flowed through validateOwnership: update-existing-key–insert-occupied-key, reject-before-deadline-consumer-requirement–retired-stake-hook-without-withdrawal, historical-non-owner-sweep and request-value-and-refund-routing depended on the state owner's signature, while retract-outside-window's retract never did (it depends only on the request owner). #79 removed the gate from Modify folding, and the 2026-09-12 operator ruling settles more: the registry has no owner role whatsoever — not latent, not transferable, not gating End or migration. state.ak's End and validateMigration still call validateOwnership; those calls are outstanding conformance defects owned by epic 17, and historical-owner-change's accepted owner change is their executed evidence.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-11
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: Superseded rows, observations preserved. historical-owner-change is resolved-by-ruling: the owner-pinning question has no premise left to be pending on, the acceptance is defect evidence, and the retired control (previous-owner End refused, new-owner accepted) tested behaviour that must not exist — it was never landed. historical-non-owner-sweep's refusal and its owner-signed control stay in the record with the conformance claim withdrawn: a gate that tests authority that does not exist discriminates nothing Singular owes. historical-owner-signed-sweep and historical-registry-termination are superseded the same way: the registry has no sweep and no termination, the end-to-end examples they cited were removed on 2026-09-12 (f3a68b1b), nothing runs either row, and list prints both uncovered. retired-stake-hook-with-withdrawal/retired-stake-hook-without-withdrawal are retired: the registry interface has no stake_script hook, so nothing runs them. The imported partition's State.stake_script hook supplies registry-owner authority by another name, which is exactly why epic 17 removes the field; the pinned staking credential cannot register anyway (the cause above), so the hook never reached a ledger. Preserved history stays unchanged, and changing applicability earns no execution credit.

the-issue-70-generic-rows.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-issue-70-generic-rows-12
the-issue-70-generic-rows.text: execution-units-and-transaction-size for this session is written from the accepting folds of update-existing-key, delete-existing-key and reinsert-deleted-key, each read off the step that folded it in its row's receipt; the other rows' worst cases live in their own receipts.

the-operation-a-fourth-constructor.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-operation-a-fourth-constructor-01
the-operation-a-fourth-constructor.text: The three published indices do not move. A read leaves its key exactly where it is, and on chain only the terminal codec byte is admitted for it.

the-registry-mode-contract-change.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-registry-mode-contract-change-01
the-registry-mode-contract-change.text: This is a contract change, declared here rather than discovered by a consumer through a failing decode. Anything that reads Singular's datums or builds its redeemers changes with it.

the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-index-00
the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.text: The request: a destination, then an edge index.

the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-index-01
the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.text: Request gained one field, appended last: destination, a pair of the binary address bytes the minted token must land at and the inline datum that output must carry, as an Option: Some carries the datum itself, None means a datum-less output. The request carries the datum rather than its hash (#419), so anyone can build the fold from the chain alone; an approval still binds the datum by its BLAKE2b-256 hash, empty for none. A request that mints nothing names no destination.

the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-index-02
the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.text: Issue #183 then re-cut the request itself. Field for field, old wire beside new:

the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-index-03
the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.text: The constructor index does not move: RequestDatum is 0 before and after, and the four unchanged fields keep their positions. What changes is what fields 3 and 4 mean.

the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-index-04
the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.text: The seven edges, with the trie move each names and the value bytes that used to carry it:

the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-index-05
the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.text: What a consumer has to change. Write the edge index where the operation payload used to go, and the deposit — the lovelace the request output holds, less the state's tip — where the tip used to go. An edge names its own leaf bytes, so a consumer no longer chooses them and can no longer get them wrong.

the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-index-06
the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.text: Refusals that go away, because no request can express them. leaf-codec (a value byte outside the three-byte codec), insert-terminal, tip-mismatch, update-to-absent, update-absent-to-terminal and update-active-to-active are all faults of value bytes that the edge wire does not carry.

the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-index-07
the-request-a-destination-then-an-edge-i.text: Refusals that remain, and the two that are new. A read whose key does not bind 0x02 is refused read-absent, read-non-terminal or key-unknown, and a tree-changing edge whose key binds 0x02 is refused edge-from-terminal — all read off the trie rather than off the request. New with this wire: edge-inadmissible for a tag outside 0-6, and deposit-mismatch for a deposit that is not the holding less the tip.

the-serialization-boundary-rows-devnet-s.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-serialization-boundary-rows-devnet-session-01
the-serialization-boundary-rows-devnet-s.text: One fresh cage per row (two where a row needs two phases), each cage booted, exercised and — except where the row says otherwise — closed on the same isolated node, in canonical order:

the-serialization-checks-that-need-no-no.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-serialization-checks-that-need-no-node-00
the-serialization-checks-that-need-no-no.text: The serialization checks that need no node.

the-serialization-checks-that-need-no-no.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-serialization-checks-that-need-no-node-01
the-serialization-checks-that-need-no-no.text: No transaction, no node, no execution units — hence mem/cpu zero and no transactions named. What is measured is stated per row, and these rows never appear in a devnet-executed count.

the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight-00
the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight.text: The state datum: six fields become eight.

the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight-01
the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight.text: consumerPin is deleted with the pinned consumer script it named; the mandatory withdrawal that script required is deleted with it. repPolicy is renamed activePolicy and keeps its meaning — the policy that mints the token standing for a live registration. Three pins are new: the application policy that certifies requests, and the absent and terminal token policies.

the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight-02
the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight.text: A decoder that reads field 4 as the representative policy now reads the application policy, and a decoder that reads six fields refuses an eight-field datum. Both are the intended consequence, and both are exercised: the state round-trip row round-trips all four derived pins through a boot datum, and its armed control demands the old six-field encoding and fails.

the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight-03
the-state-datum-six-fields-become-eight.text: None of the four is a literal. Each is derived, for the registry identity a boot creates, from the two partitions' script-identity.json: the application policy is the naming application script's applied hash, and the three token policies are the one parametrised witness script applied at kinds 0, 1 and 2.

the-state-datum-two-pins-leave.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-state-datum-two-pins-leave-00
the-state-datum-two-pins-leave.text: The state datum: two pins leave.

the-state-datum-two-pins-leave.name: docs-consumer-conformance/the-state-datum-two-pins-leave-01
the-state-datum-two-pins-leave.text: Milestone one admits only registration and permanent termination, so nothing is ever minted under the absent or the terminal token policy. The datum drops fields 6 and 7, absentPolicy and terminalPolicy, and keeps the first six fields in the order of the table above. The fold no longer preserves or checks a mint under either policy, and the witness script admits the active kind only. A registry made under the eight-field contract has another state script hash and is served by the releases that made it. A decoder that reads eight fields refuses a six-field datum.

update-and-termination-journeys-the-prev.name: docs-consumer-conformance/update-and-termination-journeys-the-previous-design-against-the-no-pin-design-00
update-and-termination-journeys-the-prev.text: Update and termination journeys: the previous design against the no-pin design.

update-and-termination-journeys-the-prev.name: docs-consumer-conformance/update-and-termination-journeys-the-previous-design-against-the-no-pin-design-01
update-and-termination-journeys-the-prev.text: As an integrator, I can follow the controller's payload update, termination booking and the fold by any wallet, and compare what each allocates under the previous design and the no-pin design. These are three owned statements in the suite's description language. They remain published uncovered because no executable comparison with the application-held model exists yet.

update-and-termination-journeys-the-prev.name: docs-consumer-conformance/update-and-termination-journeys-the-previous-design-against-the-no-pin-design-02
update-and-termination-journeys-the-prev.text: The two money changes are explicit: the protected deposit goes to the treasury when termination is booked, and the folder receives the termination request's whole value at the fold. The whole value is the gross allocation; ordinary wallet funding and the ledger fee are accounted for separately. The old carrier payment is not renamed a deposit, and the new folder payment is not limited to a declared tip.

update-and-termination-journeys-the-prev.name: docs-consumer-conformance/update-and-termination-journeys-the-previous-design-against-the-no-pin-design-03
update-and-termination-journeys-the-prev.text: The rows name OpenDatumApplicationHeld.Money.oldAllocation and OpenDatumApplicationHeld.Money.newAllocation, the update and termination journey statements, and journey_allocations. Their published state still comes from the suite's receipts. The hosted registration journey now continues through the update and termination, and the termination refusal job submits malformed attempts beside passing packaged controls. They read the development network's chain record and the node's answers. This is a separate evidence boundary: those runs establish what they execute and nothing about agreement with the model.

what-a-reader-should-do.name: docs-consumer-conformance/what-a-reader-should-do-01
what-a-reader-should-do.text: Read tokens, never the root. The presence of an active witness under the active policy, at the asset name equal to the registry key, is a live registration; a name that is over is a leaf proved terminal against the root. The asset name is the key itself — there is no hashed representative name any more.

what-backs-these-statements.name: docs-consumer-conformance/what-backs-these-statements-01
what-backs-these-statements.text: Each of the four rows reads uncovered, with the reason that no executable comparison with the application-held model exists yet. Two hosted jobs, the registration journey and the registration refusals, run the packaged commands on a development network and read the chain's own record. They are a separate evidence boundary: they establish what they run and nothing about agreement with the model. A row changes state only when a run receipt for it exists.

adopted-behavior.name: docs-decisions/adopted-behavior-01
adopted-behavior.text: These requirements incorporate the later action-asset and executing-witness corrections. Earlier alternatives requiring a second native Insert/Withdraw request policy are superseded. Policy identity and application spending-script identity remain distinct semantic roles even when an implementation shares a script hash.

decisions-and-executable-abstractions.name: docs-decisions/decisions-and-executable-abstractions-01
decisions-and-executable-abstractions.text: Historical design. This page records the earlier Insert/Update/Delete design and its broader broader model successor. The active permanent permanent contract model supports only insertActive and updateTerminal. Historical tags 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 encode refused actions, not available features. Current supported behavior describes permanent contract; archived source and evidence remain on preserve/m2/pre-m1-source-removal.

decisions-and-executable-abstractions.name: docs-decisions/decisions-and-executable-abstractions-02
decisions-and-executable-abstractions.text: As an application designer, use these decisions to distinguish behavior you can explore from construction choices you still need to settle. A successful modeled transition satisfies the selected logical checks; a refusal exposes a failed obligation. Neither result chooses your deployed scripts or proves your application policy.

decisions-and-executable-abstractions.name: docs-decisions/decisions-and-executable-abstractions-03
decisions-and-executable-abstractions.text: The reviewed behavioral baseline is the protocol specification, responsibilities, lifecycle, certification boundary and naming walkthrough. The executable candidate adds an executable interpretation for review. It does not close the construction decisions below.

evidence-and-next-stage.name: docs-decisions/evidence-and-next-stage-01
evidence-and-next-stage.text: The candidate's Lean build with its compiled axiom gate, exact proof inventory, exported finite corpus and browser checks are creator evidence. Every theorem is PROVED from the standard axioms. Independent audit, accepted statements and production conformance have not been commissioned as part of this delivery.

proposed-abstraction-boundary.name: docs-decisions/proposed-abstraction-boundary-01
proposed-abstraction-boundary.text: An executable logical map may stand for authenticated MPF state, a tagged structured value may stand for an unambiguous action commitment, and an explicit witness or contract parameter may stand for a ledger validator's authenticated result. These abstractions make the intended transition law inspectable without choosing a serialization, hash function, script deployment or application policy. Their exact use and limitations are recorded beside the Lean definitions and in the model ledger.

proposed-abstraction-boundary.name: docs-decisions/proposed-abstraction-boundary-02
proposed-abstraction-boundary.text: Required native output parameters remain explicit fields such as representative identity and quantity, datum, destination and supported value requirements. The model is not authority to introduce a universal transaction-predicate language. Example names, addresses and policy identities are illustrative values, not production schemas or a global allowlist.

proposed-abstraction-boundary.name: docs-decisions/proposed-abstraction-boundary-03
proposed-abstraction-boundary.text: The desired identity is one canonical registry per application policy ID, without an arbitrary independent instance parameter. The policy can serve as a downstream trust anchor, conditional on its issuance invariants, but parameterizing by that reusable ID does not prevent duplicate creation of the same registry asset and state. Bootstrap must enforce an at-most-once invariant. An asset is identified by policy ID and asset name; a policy ID alone identifies a distinguished singleton only when its issuance rules enforce that distinction. An application-supplied one-shot bootstrap certificate could avoid a separate Singular nonce parameter; consuming a nonce UTxO is another construction option. The bootstrap mechanism remains open as part of configuration and registry identity construction. The current model starts with a supplied Config and contains no registry-creation transition, so it establishes neither bootstrap enforcement nor deployed registry uniqueness.

proposed-abstraction-boundary.name: docs-decisions/proposed-abstraction-boundary-04
proposed-abstraction-boundary.text: The diagram separates the desired identity from the unresolved enforcement mechanism. The current executable model supplies configuration after this boundary; it does not model either bootstrap option.

demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-.name: docs-demo1/demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-termination-00
demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-.text: Demo 1: play a registry from creation to termination.

demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-.name: docs-demo1/demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-termination-01
demo-1-play-a-registry-from-creation-to-.text: As a Cardano developer who knows wallets, faucets and Koios but has never used Singular, you want to watch a registry work before you read how it is built: a registry is created, a key is put in it, changed and ended, the registry refuses what it must refuse, and two people sign their writes in two different ways. Demo 1 is that play, in sixteen steps. The steps, and the programs to run them, live in a repository of their own, singular-demo. This page says what the play shows and where to play it.

the-release-behind-it.name: docs-demo1/the-release-behind-it-01
the-release-behind-it.text: The play runs a release of Singular. These pages are about the release itself, not about the steps: install the commands without Nix and download and verify a release.

what-it-does-not-claim.name: docs-demo1/what-it-does-not-claim-01
what-it-does-not-claim.text: Everything the step-by-step page runs happens on a private test chain that it starts; nothing touches a public network. The open datum application protects the payload and the deposit and nothing more: it demonstrates the registry's mechanics. The receipts of a play are evidence of behaviour on a private chain only, and no complete conformance is claimed here. What the project does claim, and what it leaves open, is on the conformance evidence page. What is deployed on the public preprod network, and the transactions the project's own journeys submitted there, are recorded in the preprod record.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-01
what-the-play-shows.text: Two people, Alice and Bob, share one registry. Its application, open datum, lets a key carry a payload that only the key's controller may replace, and keeps a deposit of 2 tADA with the key until the key is terminated.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-02
what-the-play-shows.text: The play creates the registry, books a key and folds it so that the key becomes active, updates its payload, books and folds the key's end, then rejects a request that nobody folded, reclaims a new one inside its retract window, and books and folds one more key.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-03
what-the-play-shows.text: A write does not change the registry at once. It books a request, which waits until someone folds it, and any wallet may fold. A request that nobody folds within its processing window can be rejected once a second window, the retract window, has also passed; inside that second window its owner can take it back. The play walks each of these, so that you see the refusals where they happen: a reject that comes too early is refused, and so is a reclaim that comes too early.

what-the-play-shows.name: docs-demo1/what-the-play-shows-04
what-the-play-shows.text: The two people sign in the two ways Singular offers. Alice names her vault, a file holding her signing key sealed by a passphrase, and one command builds, signs and sends. Bob names only his wallet's address and a bundle file: the command builds the transactions into the file, signs nothing, and exits with status 19, which means it is waiting for signatures. Then Bob signs the bundle from his vault and sends it, so the machine that builds a write never needs to hold the key.

where-to-play-it.name: docs-demo1/where-to-play-it-01
where-to-play-it.text: Every way below plays the same sixteen steps. The table lists five: the recorded run to watch, the Killercoda scenario to play in a browser, the step-by-step page to paste from, which needs the programs, and the Nix shell and the Ubuntu kit, which are two ways to get the programs. To play on your own machine, start with the step-by-step page.

where-to-play-it.name: docs-demo1/where-to-play-it-02
where-to-play-it.text: The singular-demo repository describes the shell and the kit, what each is pinned to and what it was tested on.

maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-p.name: docs-demos-d02-naming/maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-preprod-target-00
maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-p.text: Maintain and recover a name — 23 October preprod target.

maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-p.name: docs-demos-d02-naming/maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-preprod-target-01
maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-p.text: As a name holder, I want to keep the same name while changing its payment destination and recovering control with my precommitted key, so that a payer can use my current destination.

maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-p.name: docs-demos-d02-naming/maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-preprod-target-02
maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-p.text: Planned release tag: Singular v2.0.0 (naming and escrow milestone). This is a milestone target; the tag waits for the 30 October release gate, a built archive and connected preprod receipts. Candidate plays do not publish it.

maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-p.name: docs-demos-d02-naming/maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-preprod-target-03
maintain-and-recover-a-name-23-october-p.text: This is a Cardano preprod target, not a completed demonstration. The presenter will use keripy kli to create and rotate the controller's KERI identity and a released ckeri command to submit and read back each connected Cardano action. The Singular naming commands and preprod release needed to join that journey are still missing. The dated project card remains a review target.

preprod-play-to-record.name: docs-demos-d02-naming/preprod-play-to-record-01
preprod-play-to-record.text: The accepted naming lifecycle model at a6e5edbc2dafa82eb34116a1de2b6503f87c6692 defines maintenance, recovery and refusals. Its synthetic address bytes and key 42 are model fixtures. They are not preprod assets, keys or transactions. The Cardano KERI to Singular registry mapping remains open in KERI #435, so the preprod sequence above cannot yet be claimed as a connected implementation.

recording-gate.name: docs-demos-d02-naming/recording-gate-01
recording-gate.text: The asciicast must record the real kli, ckeri and Singular commands and their preprod readbacks. Invented identities may be generated for the demo, but their actual AID, asset IDs, transaction IDs and refusals must come from that run. No preprod cast is attached yet. The earlier Lean and Node recording is model evidence and does not demonstrate this user story.

recording-gate.name: docs-demos-d02-naming/recording-gate-02
recording-gate.text: The Singular naming epic must supply the released naming interface and transaction path. The Cardano KERI registry mapping must bind the two accepted models before connected acceptance. Until then, the page is a play plan, with no claim of naming preprod acceptance.

missing-interface-and-evidence.name: docs-demos-d03-escrow/missing-interface-and-evidence-01
missing-interface-and-evidence.text: The escrow validator ticket, CLI ticket, preprod journey and completion repair must yield one connected runnable script from a downloaded release. This page has no release or preprod receipt, and the two claims and three refusals have not been observed here. No timeout, refund route or payer privilege is inferred.

name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-oct.name: docs-demos-d03-escrow/name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-october-target-00
name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-oct.text: Name Your Address preprod stretch — 30 October target.

name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-oct.name: docs-demos-d03-escrow/name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-october-target-01
name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-oct.text: As Bob, I want to lock funds against the ordered names Alice then Bob, so Alice can claim at her current destination after recovery and I can claim only after Alice's name ends permanently. This dated project card is not yet playable as a connected preprod journey.

name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-oct.name: docs-demos-d03-escrow/name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-october-target-02
name-your-address-preprod-stretch-30-oct.text: Planned release tag: Singular v2.0.0 (naming and escrow milestone). This is a milestone target; the tag waits for the 30 October release gate, a built archive and connected preprod receipts. Candidate plays do not publish it.

planned-play.name: docs-demos-d03-escrow/planned-play-01
planned-play.text: The accepted Singular model at a6e5edbc2dafa82eb34116a1de2b6503f87c6692 supplies the registry edges and naming lifecycle. Their synthetic model address bytes are not a preprod wallet. The 23 October naming play is also awaiting connected kli, ckeri and Singular commands. There is no cast of an accepted preprod escrow payment here.

choose-a-dated-play.name: docs-demos-index/choose-a-dated-play-01
choose-a-dated-play.text: The Cardano KERI consumer mapping is separate from Singular naming. Naming is not a prerequisite for Cardano KERI's identity path.

dated-demo-plays.name: docs-demos-index/dated-demo-plays-01
dated-demo-plays.text: As a presenter, I want each dated play to show a keripy kli identity and a ckeri transaction on Cardano preprod, so that the audience can inspect the identity event and ledger result together. A cast appears only after the connected preprod run has produced transaction IDs and fresh readbacks.

dated-demo-plays.name: docs-demos-index/dated-demo-plays-02
dated-demo-plays.text: For Cardano KERI identity actions, the planned source is its local follower indexer: ckeri writes use --store PATH or CKERI_STORE, and reads use explicit --backend local --store PATH (or an indexer-backed endpoint where supported). Record the indexed chain point and freshness. Singular's ordinary path now reads raw outputs and history through Koios; its logical sessions are Unbound and its facts Unverified, and #107 tracks a persistent registry follower. A Koios asset lookup alone does not close these demo stories. The Cardano KERI indexer contract tracks the identity side. The older V1 cast used Koios and remains historical evidence.

planned-major-release-tags.name: docs-demos-index/planned-major-release-tags-01
planned-major-release-tags.text: Demo 1 ships in the 0.x series; the latest release is listed at https://github.com/lambdasistemi/singular/releases/latest. The major tags below were drafted before that decision. They are targets for the later plays, not published artifacts.

planned-major-release-tags.name: docs-demos-index/planned-major-release-tags-02
planned-major-release-tags.text: Candidate demos cite their actual build and manifest until the relevant milestone release is cut.

candidate-status.name: docs-design/candidate-status-01
candidate-status.text: The same published candidate includes the executable Lean source, proved statements, their supporting lemmas and exported finite corpus. Their identity belongs to this candidate; the proofs were completed without changing any statement.

candidate-status.name: docs-design/candidate-status-02
candidate-status.text: The repository carries no deployed Singular validator, accepted statement audit or production release. The proofs are complete and individually inventoried, with a compiled axiom gate on every build. The requested review surface is the draft PR and its exact candidate preview; independent audit stages remain separate work.

candidate-status.name: docs-design/candidate-status-03
candidate-status.text: Two blind source reviews preceded simulator authoring and both recommended proceeding. Their source reasoning did not execute an audit or prove the model. The resulting corpus refinements preserve the reviewed model and statement definitions. The general whole-transition terminal-custody theorem remains an explicit statement-coverage gap in the model ledger.

candidate-status.name: docs-design/candidate-status-04
candidate-status.text: The original protocol specification remains the behavioral authority. Its statements about unexecuted obligations describe the adopted specification baseline; executable coverage introduced in this candidate is tracked in the model ledger rather than inferred from a successful documentation build.

executable-design-candidate.name: docs-design/executable-design-candidate-01
executable-design-candidate.text: Historical design. This page records the earlier Insert/Update/Delete design and its broader broader model successor. The active permanent permanent contract model supports only insertActive and updateTerminal. Historical tags 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 encode refused actions, not available features. Current supported behavior describes permanent contract; archived source and evidence remain on preserve/m2/pre-m1-source-removal.

executable-design-candidate.name: docs-design/executable-design-candidate-02
executable-design-candidate.text: As an application designer, follow a registration from an approved request into a live application output, then explore address changes, retirement and deletion. The simulator shows successful transitions and exact refusals so you can inspect the proposed behavior before choosing a ledger construction.

executable-design-candidate.name: docs-design/executable-design-candidate-03
executable-design-candidate.text: Open the playable Singular simulator — the live generic-registry simulator, where Delete is allowed — or follow the simulation walkthrough.

executable-design-candidate.name: docs-design/executable-design-candidate-04
executable-design-candidate.text: This is a creation candidate: the logical Lean model and separately authored browser simulation make the design executable. All 65 theorem and inversion declarations — 44 for the registry, 7 for the naming instance, 9 for its lifecycle and 5 for its wire encoding, counts the model check derives from the manifests — are PROVED from the standard axioms, and the build refuses any statement that is admitted again. Proofs establish properties of the model; they do not by themselves accept the design.

reading-the-application-trust-boundary.name: docs-design/reading-the-application-trust-boundary-01
reading-the-application-trust-boundary.text: The model uses logical identities and authenticated state instead of Cardano bytes and MPF proofs. Application authorization is an explicit contract boundary: recognizing the configured issuer does not establish that an arbitrary application's policy implements the semantics it claims.

reading-the-application-trust-boundary.name: docs-design/reading-the-application-trust-boundary-02
reading-the-application-trust-boundary.text: The model supplies authenticated application evidence; the browser does not execute those validators. The decisions and executable abstractions distinguish adopted behavior from unresolved construction choices.

reading-the-application-trust-boundary.name: docs-design/reading-the-application-trust-boundary-03
reading-the-application-trust-boundary.text: The simulation is a separate author's transcription of the frozen Lean interface. Its clarity record preserves what the formal artifacts did and did not communicate. Finite trace agreement and interactive checks provide bounded creator evidence. They cannot establish universal correspondence, an independent statement audit, proof completeness or ledger deployment conformance.

story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-term.name: docs-design/story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-terminal-request-00
story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-term.text: Story: cancel a proposal or finish a terminal request.

story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-term.name: docs-design/story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-terminal-request-01
story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-term.text: A requester can cancel a pending Insert only with a separately authorized Withdraw action bound to that exact request and declared refund requirements. The original Insert approval is insufficient. Withdrawal creates no representative and changes no registry entry; refund commitments do not establish a wallet payment.

story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-term.name: docs-design/story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-terminal-request-02
story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-term.text: For retirement or deletion, the application validator authorizes the exact terminal request and releases its existing representative into request custody. The registry stays Active, but the representative is unavailable to the application. No ordinary cancellation or sweep releases it. Valid completion consumes the request, burns the representative and changes the map.

story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-term.name: docs-design/story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-terminal-request-03
story-cancel-a-proposal-or-finish-a-term.text: These are executable behaviors and proved obligations. A general whole-transition theorem that terminal custody leaves only through completion is still missing. Escape-refusal and supply statements, or a finite terminal-Withdraw refusal, do not close that gap.

story-fold-a-selected-batch.name: docs-design/story-fold-a-selected-batch-01
story-fold-a-selected-batch.text: Any submitter can select an ordered batch. Each item sees the registry produced by the previous item; a failure refuses the selected batch atomically. There is no native privileged folder gate, automatic skipping, capacity guarantee or fairness claim. Executing witnesses remain required even when mint and burn quantities for the same asset net to zero; distinct identities do not cancel each other.

story-fold-a-selected-batch.name: docs-design/story-fold-a-selected-batch-02
story-fold-a-selected-batch.text: The model ledger maps requirements and finite scenarios to modeled behavior, conditions, abstractions and omissions. The theorem inventory records the exact statements, each proved. The mutation ledger records four executed mutants, each killed at a named obligation; no survivor census or independent audit result is claimed.

story-register-and-use-an-application-ou.name: docs-design/story-register-and-use-an-application-output-00
story-register-and-use-an-application-ou.text: Story: register and use an application output.

story-register-and-use-an-application-ou.name: docs-design/story-register-and-use-an-application-output-01
story-register-and-use-an-application-ou.text: A requester stages a certified Insert whose approval binds the initial application output. Staging reserves no key and creates no representative. At fold time, the key must be absent and the exact output and approval scope must match. A valid Insert creates the representative and makes the entry Active; a competing Insert at an occupied key is refused.

story-register-and-use-an-application-ou.name: docs-design/story-register-and-use-an-application-output-02
story-register-and-use-an-application-ou.text: The diagram shows registry states. Staging a pending Insert does not change whether the key is absent. An application can evolve its own state while preserving its representative; changing an address is such an evolution. Registry Update means retirement, and Over has no outgoing transition. Delete makes the key absent again; any reinsert still needs a valid certified output and approval scope for its incarnation.

checked-declaration-register.name: docs-economics-paper/checked-declaration-register-01
checked-declaration-register.text: The entries below are generated from a fresh run of lake env lean tools/axioms.lean over the pinned source, with every cited name confirmed by git show at that revision. Each row uses the full revision above and quotes its axiom line verbatim. Standard axioms are printed as observed; none of these entries contains an additional axiom or sorryAx. Definitions and supplied hand arguments are distinguished from checked declarations in the paper.

checked-declaration-register.name: docs-economics-paper/checked-declaration-register-02
checked-declaration-register.text: The axiom report digest is d22520a04f196bfe52e69ac18d156cce82c78d34f4a6365a16a2138a2815a2f9. The trusted base includes Lean's kernel and the printed axioms, specification adequacy, authentic ledger observations, application authorization and the unproved model-to-validator correspondence. Executable commitment functions are stand-ins; tag counts do not establish cryptographic binding.

every-exit-and-every-amount.name: docs-economics-paper/every-exit-and-every-amount-01
every-exit-and-every-amount.text: Existing checked declaration: fold routing separates state continuation, exact carrier outputs, donation and ordinary funding. With ordinary inputs I, ordinary outputs O, total tips T and ledger fee f, it proves O + f = I + T and f ≤ I. Donation equals the registration costs plus held-minus-tip for every termination. Ordinary change remains a separate output even at a carrier's address. Ordinary funding and change are lovelace only: the fold and retraction both refuse an unrelated native asset.

every-exit-and-every-amount.name: docs-economics-paper/every-exit-and-every-amount-02
every-exit-and-every-amount.text: Hand proof supplied: subtracting in the integers gives O − I = T − f. If the processor owns the ordinary funding pool and no other role, that is its monetary net before external costs. It is not a wealth statement about every address receiving an output. The paper's separate net-payoff table includes the booking fee, destination carrier and treasury donation; its rows sum to minus ledger fees, not to request holdings.

every-exit-and-every-amount.name: docs-economics-paper/every-exit-and-every-amount-03
every-exit-and-every-amount.text: Rejection refunds are added per address, with distinct request inputs and one shared interval. A repeated input or one live compatible member refuses the entire batch. A fold that lands first spends the referenced state output, so an in-flight rejection must be rebuilt; no starvation bound is proved.

every-exit-and-every-amount.name: docs-economics-paper/every-exit-and-every-amount-04
every-exit-and-every-amount.text: A zero donation omits the field. Conway transaction-body field 22 accepts a positive donation; optional field 21 is the separate current-treasury assertion. Donation alone does not assert the current treasury balance. The paper cites the exact Conway CDDL revision and its treasury-value check.

future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.name: docs-economics-paper/future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-evidence-00
future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.text: Future work: reusable names and durable evidence.

future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.name: docs-economics-paper/future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-evidence-01
