future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.text: Proposed statement: non-terminality. Deleting an active key would let an application reuse its name. This is a proposed extension to a different lifecycle contract, not a way to undo termination in an existing permanent registry.

future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.name: docs-economics-paper/future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-evidence-02
future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.text: Proposed statement: proof durability through witnesses. The other four proposed edges would create an absent witness, change that absent state to active, delete the absent state, and mint a terminal witness on demand. A separate presence witness would be minted with a name's token and burned when the name is terminated or deleted. Absence, presence and termination would then each have an attestation token. These five edges and the presence witness are proposed, not proved functionality of the active contract.

future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.name: docs-economics-paper/future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-evidence-03
future-work-reusable-names-and-durable-e.text: Hand proof supplied: a transaction referencing the application output holding a name's token loses that input when an application update spends it. A proof against the current registry root similarly depends on a state output that another fold may spend. The goal of the proposed witnesses is to make such evidence more durable. Missing mechanization: their minting, invalidation, custody and verification rules need a future model and implementation evidence. Presence and absence cannot be promised valid after their conditions cease to hold.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-01
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Existing checked declarations: Singular.Statements.retraction_pays_only_the_refund_and_the_fee proves full refund, zero donation, unchanged treasury, fee covered by ordinary funding and balance. If I is that funding, f the fee and P all outputs elsewhere than the refund address, then P ≤ I − f. The model has no wallet-ownership or output-purpose observation: other-address change and third-party payment are indistinguishable, but neither can consume the request's cost or tip. Singular.Statements.pending_registration_can_be_retracted proves existence with explicit reachable-world, pending-request, nonempty-window, signing and funding premises. Neither theorem supplies wallet funds, ledger minima, builder success or inclusion.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-02
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Hand proof supplied: a request holding 3,000,000 lovelace cannot alone return that amount and pay a 170,000 fee. With 200,000 ordinary funding, the model's construction returns 3,030,000 to the refund address and balances. If the requester owns the refund and funding, its net loss is the booking fee plus the retraction fee, with no processor or treasury allocation. These numbers illustrate the checked construction under its premises, not measured ledger costs.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-03
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Hand proof supplied: conditional rejection cap. The refund promise is a floor, not an exact split; a processor may leave some tip to the requester. If the transaction additionally balances with zero donation, all outputs outside its refund addresses plus its fee total at most the tips. The paper derives this bound from the summed floors and names balance as an extra premise. Its exact-refund net-payoff illustration is also conditional, not a claim about every accepted rejection.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-04
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Hand proof supplied: a self-rejecting funder can make the tip an internal transfer, so the design has no universal treasury flood price. Successful junk folds still pay R and occupy turns. Two registrations can race for one key; the loser retains its refund floor, not priority or ownership. A processor's fee can exceed the tip. A rejection sharing a request input with a proposed fold can invalidate that fold despite preserving the state output. Repeated folds can invalidate rejection references indefinitely.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-05
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: Proposed statement: the minimum tip should cover measured singleton costs within a declared ledger envelope. The paper derives conditional inequalities for costs and windows, without assuming a minimum service rate or full batches. No measurements establish the selected registration cost, minimum tip or booking-width bound. A later fee or output-minimum change can invalidate the envelope.

limitations-and-counterexamples.name: docs-economics-paper/limitations-and-counterexamples-06
limitations-and-counterexamples.text: The application's release rule and custody integration, the open-datum adaptation, the cardano-keri adaptation and validator/builder correspondence with live receipts remain open. The singular tag's fate is decided: mint and delivery on registration, movement at termination booking, burn at termination fold. No key-ownership, squatting, inclusion, priority or application-security guarantee follows from Singular's token counts.

named.name: docs-economics-paper/named-01
named.text: Each token has a name: registering a name mints exactly one token for it, and the registry is the only way to mint it. Holding the token is holding the name. The story is a registered name represented by a token an application holds with its own payload.

named.name: docs-economics-paper/named-02
named.text: Existing checked declaration: Singular.Statements.insert_active_transaction_row describes the original registry's one minted active asset, its key-derived model name and its destination holding. Singular.Statements.world_supply_sync counts the economic world's actual singular tags across application custody and pending terminations. The register below supplies the exact pin and axiom lines. Missing mechanization: the actual minting policy and name encoding need correspondence evidence; holding the representative proves no legal right or personal identity.

named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.name: docs-economics-paper/named-unique-permanent-permissionless-and-reusable-00
named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.text: Named, unique, permanent; permissionless and reusable.

named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.name: docs-economics-paper/named-unique-permanent-permissionless-and-reusable-01
named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.text: Singular is a permissionless and reusable mint of named, unique and permanent tokens on Cardano. This is the adopted definition and the paper's organizing promise. The five meanings below distinguish checked model results from application goals and demonstrations.

named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.name: docs-economics-paper/named-unique-permanent-permissionless-and-reusable-02
named-unique-permanent-permissionless-an.text: Cardano KERI motivates checkpoints selectable by KERI identifier and evidence of whether an identifier was ever convicted on Cardano. For KERI a conviction is a termination, and it is permanent. A lookup of an identifier at a registry root has three outcomes. An active leaf proves that the identifier is registered and not convicted at that root: “not convicted” means active. A terminal leaf proves conviction. An unknown leaf proves only that the identifier is not registered on Singular; that is a different answer and is never presented as “not convicted”. The stored Absent leaf belongs to the extension edges outside the contract of the first release and is not part of this reading. Existing checked declaration: Singular.Statements.termination keeps a terminal leaf terminal through every later accepted batch, and Singular.Statements.terminal_attestation_permanent keeps a held terminal attestation held and its leaf terminal. Hand proof supplied: by induction over the accepted batches from the genesis state, a key terminal at one reachable state is terminal at every later one, so an active leaf at a root shows the key was never terminal before it: an active identifier was never convicted before that root. Missing mechanization: the lookup is a logical read of the root and verifying a concrete lookup proof is a correspondence obligation; a lookup is valid only against the current root until the next fold; durable attestations are future work, proposed and not proved; Singular alone does not verify duplicity or establish a KERI history, and the consumer integration remains open.

permanent.name: docs-economics-paper/permanent-01
permanent.text: Terminating a name burns its token and records it as terminal; it can never be issued again. Alice terminates her name, then tries to register it again and is refused. For KERI, termination is intended to be conviction: the convicted identifier must never come back in that registry.

permanent.name: docs-economics-paper/permanent-02
permanent.text: Hand proof supplied: read as a lookup, a terminal leaf proves conviction and an active leaf at a reachable root shows the key was never terminal before it; an unknown leaf proves only that the identifier is not registered. Existing checked declaration: Singular.Statements.termination refuses requests at a terminal key in a reachable original registry and preserves its terminal leaf through later accepted batches. Singular.Statements.booked_termination_foldable supplies a conditional economic fold making the key terminal, and Singular.Statements.world_supply_sync then gives zero supply. Missing mechanization: KERI's conviction and custody release require application evidence. The economic termination donates everything held except the tip, as Singular.Statements.fold_routes_every_amount states; Alice receives no deposit back.

permissionless.name: docs-economics-paper/permissionless-01
permissionless.text: Anyone creates a registry, anyone books a name, anyone settles pending requests, all from public chain data. The creator has no power over the names. These participation promises remain subject to application authorization, funding and admission. Bob, who did not create the registry, settles pending requests, Alice's included.

permissionless.name: docs-economics-paper/permissionless-02
permissionless.text: Existing checked declarations: Singular.Statements.fold_inputs_public equates the original builder with construction from its public view; Singular.Statements.fold_requires_no_signer proves empty required signers and invariance under changed approval signatures. Missing mechanization: these are original-builder results, not an economic-builder public-data theorem or a running demonstration. Creation, chain-data retrieval and Bob's actual batch require off-chain and validator evidence. No inclusion guarantee follows.

requests-tokens-and-clocks.name: docs-economics-paper/requests-tokens-and-clocks-01
requests-tokens-and-clocks.text: Let R be the registration cost, t the declared tip, and a the declared carrier lovelace. Booking enforces the fixed minimum tip. The carrier amount follows actual ledger minimum rules; the model proves exact declared amounts and does not compute those minima.

requests-tokens-and-clocks.name: docs-economics-paper/requests-tokens-and-clocks-02
requests-tokens-and-clocks.text: A registration's application tag commits to its payload and nonce; its trie-ready tag commits to the operation and the same nonce. Both are minted in the same booking and burned on every exit. Application tags minted elsewhere are outside Singular's supply guarantee and cannot substitute for this booking. Termination booking moves the singular tag from custody; its fold burns that tag and the trie-ready tag. A registration fold mints the singular tag at the booked destination with the declared carrier and datum.

requests-tokens-and-clocks.name: docs-economics-paper/requests-tokens-and-clocks-03
requests-tokens-and-clocks.text: The fixed parameters are registration cost, minimum tip, maximum booking width, processing and reclaim windows, policy bindings and registry identity. The minimum tip retains the wire key maxFee. There is no parameter-update or migration authority. The paper treats the maximum booking width being smaller than the processing window as a sizing criterion, distinct from the checked booking-width bound.

reusable.name: docs-economics-paper/reusable-01
reusable.text: The same mint serves any application: open-datum today, a closed variant in the demonstration, KERI checkpoints next, with no change to its contract. Each name's token lives in its owner's application, which decides what the name points to.

reusable.name: docs-economics-paper/reusable-02
reusable.text: Missing mechanization: the concrete application demonstration uses a closed flag on the same release and commands. It sets the payload at registration, refuses every update and leaves only termination. This is application-validator and executable behavior outside the checked registry model; this paper asserts no release or running-demonstration receipt. KERI integration and serving both application kinds in one registry through application tags remain future work.

singular-registry-design-and-economics.name: docs-economics-paper/singular-registry-design-and-economics-01
singular-registry-design-and-economics.text: As a reviewer, read this page to learn what a registration or termination commits, where its tokens and lovelace go, and which promises have checked evidence. The paper explains the complete mechanism, its assumptions and its counterexamples: download the paper PDF. The documentation build compiles the PDF from the committed LaTeX sources using the llncs class.

singular-registry-design-and-economics.name: docs-economics-paper/singular-registry-design-and-economics-02
singular-registry-design-and-economics.text: Implementation standing: not yet conformant. The validators and builders still implement superseded economic rules. The conformance evidence keeps affected requirements unmet; a Lean proof is not a ledger receipt or deployment acceptance.

the-mechanism-at-a-glance.name: docs-economics-paper/the-mechanism-at-a-glance-01
the-mechanism-at-a-glance.text: The registry records a permanent lifecycle. Registration changes an unknown key to active; termination changes an active key to terminal. The application authorizes registration and controls the resulting singular tag. It consents to termination by releasing that genuine tag into a request. Singular does not judge the application's release rule. Checked lifecycle and custody evidence appears in the declaration register below.

the-mechanism-at-a-glance.name: docs-economics-paper/the-mechanism-at-a-glance-02
the-mechanism-at-a-glance.text: Pending requests occupy their own outputs. Folds spend and continue the registry state output. Rejection reads that output by reference and spends only the rejected registrations. It needs a current lifecycle mismatch or expiry after both registration windows. Compatible registrations are protected through the reclaim window; a lost race can create a mismatch earlier. A termination has no rejection, retraction or expiry exit.

unique.name: docs-economics-paper/unique-01
unique.text: A name can be taken only with a proof that it is absent, so two people cannot hold separate genuine tokens for the same name in one registry. Bob tries to register Alice's already registered name and is refused.

unique.name: docs-economics-paper/unique-02
unique.text: Existing checked declaration: Singular.Statements.insert_active_transaction_row refuses a subsequent approved registration of the same key with key-exists. Singular.Statements.world_supply_sync bounds economic supply by one, including a token in a pending termination. Missing mechanization: actual absence-proof verification is a validator correspondence obligation. “Absent” in this story means unknown and untaken, not the historical stored Absent leaf. Booking does not reserve a name or establish who ought to own it.

what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.name: docs-economics-paper/what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength-00
what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.text: What is checked, and at what strength.

what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.name: docs-economics-paper/what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength-01
what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.text: Existing checked declaration means the register below quotes the declaration's fresh axiom result at the exact model pin. Hand proof supplied means the paper gives an argument and its premises. Proposed statement means a conditional design or sizing criterion. Missing mechanization marks an unproved boundary. These four labels do not imply implementation conformance.

what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.name: docs-economics-paper/what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength-02
what-is-checked-and-at-what-strength.text: The exact model revision is 4254a3073fe0457946eba0a68d974c999c930ebf, the last ancestor commit changing the model, checked with Lean 4.27.0. Economic reachability starts from any reachable original registry with empty pending pools and a zero treasury counter, then admits bookings, rejections, retractions and economic folds. It does not claim a complete economic history from ledger genesis.

first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.name: docs-first-demo/first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod-00
first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.text: First demo: registry handoff on preprod.

first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.name: docs-first-demo/first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod-01
first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.text: As a Cardano KERI integrator, I want to see a released Singular registry handle a real identity's registration, retirement and custody, so that I can evaluate the interface that Cardano KERI will consume.

first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.name: docs-first-demo/first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod-02
first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.text: Where this stands (October 2026). The registry half of this play, called Demo 1, can be played today on a private test chain: the Demo 1 page says what it shows and links the steps to play. The play below, which joins a kli identity and ckeri, is the later integration. It was planned before Demo 1 was cut, so its dates and its release tag are plans, not results: Demo 1 ships in the 0.x series, and the v1.0.0 tag this page once named is not the tag Demo 1 uses.

first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.name: docs-first-demo/first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod-03
first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.text: 8 October 2026 was a target, not an observed result. The project story requires a connected Cardano preprod play. The accepted Singular Lean model defines expected transitions; the deployed script, released operator command and fresh node readbacks must establish each claimed outcome.

first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.name: docs-first-demo/first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod-04
first-demo-registry-handoff-on-preprod.text: The planned identity read path is the Cardano KERI follower store: use ckeri writes with --store PATH and status with explicit --backend local --store PATH, recording its chain point and freshness. The Singular registry readback needs the persistent indexed proof path tracked by #107; the current ordinary Koios path provides raw outputs and history in Unbound sessions with Unverified facts, without that accepted persistent proof path. The older Koios-backed V1 cast is a checkpoint baseline only; it cannot stand in for this joined result.

preprod-play-to-record.name: docs-first-demo/preprod-play-to-record-01
preprod-play-to-record.text: The registry operation names above describe the user story. They are not asserted to be commands available in the current release. The registry epic #154 must supply the released Singular interface and connected preprod receipts. The Cardano KERI consumer mapping #324 must bind the two accepted models before the joined sequence is an accepted integration.

recording-gate.name: docs-first-demo/recording-gate-01
recording-gate.text: Record an asciicast only after the exact kli, ckeri and Singular preprod commands complete. The cast must show their real output, transaction IDs, script and policy identities and fresh readbacks. A fictional name may label a freshly generated identity or asset, but its actual identifiers and ledger effects must come from the run. No preprod cast is attached yet.

how-a-release-gets-its-bundles.name: docs-install/how-a-release-gets-its-bundles-00
how-a-release-gets-its-bundles.text: How a release gets its bundles.

how-a-release-gets-its-bundles.name: docs-install/how-a-release-gets-its-bundles-01
how-a-release-gets-its-bundles.text: As a maintainer, you want a release to publish only bundles that were already built and run on their own platform, so that a broken platform is found in a pull request and never after the tag.

how-a-release-gets-its-bundles.name: docs-install/how-a-release-gets-its-bundles-02
how-a-release-gets-its-bundles.text: The Linux bundle is built on the self-hosted runner and the macOS bundle on a GitHub-hosted Apple Silicon runner, each from the release-bundle output of the repository's flake. A bundle failing on either platform fails the release before anything is published, and the publisher refuses a release that lacks a bundle for any platform listed in tools/release_bundles.sh. Nothing in a pull request publishes: the built tarballs are kept as workflow artifacts for a week.

how-a-release-gets-its-bundles.name: docs-install/how-a-release-gets-its-bundles-03
how-a-release-gets-its-bundles.text: The Linux packages and the Homebrew formula follow the organisation's shared release actions and Nix helpers (dev-assets). A pull request builds the AppImages, the DEB and the RPM, runs every command from each one unpacked, and then installs the DEB on Ubuntu and the RPM on Fedora and runs each AppImage, on machines without Nix. It also builds the formula from the macOS tarball, installs it through a local tap that points at that tarball, and runs brew test. The release tag publishes the Linux packages once the release exists. The formula follows once verify-release has passed: it is pushed to the organisation's tap only if the release's macOS tarball is the one the formula names, then installed from the tap and tested. A manual run of the bundles workflow can publish the dev channels: the dev-linux packages and the singular-dev formula.

install-on-linux.name: docs-install/install-on-linux-01
install-on-linux.text: You need curl, tar and sha256sum, which every distribution carries. The programs bring their own C library and do not use the distribution's.

install-on-macos.name: docs-install/install-on-macos-01
install-on-macos.text: macOS ships curl, tar and shasum. The command is the same with the platform and the checksum tool changed.

install-on-macos.name: docs-install/install-on-macos-02
install-on-macos.text: The programs are signed ad hoc, which Apple Silicon requires of any program, and are not signed with an Apple developer certificate or notarised. A file downloaded with curl and unpacked with tar is not quarantined and runs. A file downloaded with a browser is quarantined, and macOS may refuse to open the programs inside it with a message that the developer cannot be verified. After you have checked the checksum, remove the quarantine mark once:

install-the-commands-without-nix.name: docs-install/install-the-commands-without-nix-01
install-the-commands-without-nix.text: You develop for Cardano on Linux or on an Apple Silicon Mac and you want to play the first demo without installing Nix or compiling the Haskell stack. On a Mac you install the commands with one Homebrew command; on Linux you install a DEB or an RPM, or run an AppImage; on either you can instead download the tarball for your platform, check it against the release's checksums and unpack it. You run singular --version and see the release and the commit the program was built from, and then run the commands of the first demo. From the release after 0.13.1 every one of these also holds the private development node the first demo starts, so that node needs no nix command either.

install-the-linux-packages.name: docs-install/install-the-linux-packages-01
install-the-linux-packages.text: For the releases after 0.13.1, a DEB or an RPM installs all three commands into /usr/bin, with everything they need, on any distribution of its family, and your package manager removes them again. An AppImage holds one command as one file you run where it lies.

install-the-linux-packages.name: docs-install/install-the-linux-packages-02
install-the-linux-packages.text: On Fedora and its relatives the RPM goes in the same way, with sudo dnf install ./singular-${version}-x86_64-linux.rpm. An AppImage, for example singular-${version}-x86_64-linux.AppImage, is made executable with chmod +x and run as ./singular-${version}-x86_64-linux.AppImage --version; it needs FUSE and user namespaces, which desktop distributions allow. The packages put their files under /nix/store and the commands in /usr/bin; they do not need Nix and do not install it.

install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac.name: docs-install/install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac-00
install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac.text: Install with Homebrew on a Mac.

install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac.name: docs-install/install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac-01
install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac.text: For the releases after 0.13.1, a Mac with Apple Silicon and Homebrew installs the latest release with one command, and brew upgrade takes the next one:

install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac.name: docs-install/install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac-02
install-with-homebrew-on-a-mac.text: Homebrew downloads the macOS tarball from the release, checks it against the checksum the formula carries and links singular, open-datum and devnet onto your path. The Cardano node stays inside the installation, where devnet finds it, so it never replaces a node you installed yourself. The formula's own test runs --version of the three commands.

other-platforms-and-the-nix-route.name: docs-install/other-platforms-and-the-nix-route-00
other-platforms-and-the-nix-route.text: Other platforms and the Nix route.

other-platforms-and-the-nix-route.name: docs-install/other-platforms-and-the-nix-route-01
other-platforms-and-the-nix-route.text: Releases carry bundles for Linux on x86_64 and macOS on Apple Silicon only. Linux on aarch64 and macOS on Intel have no bundle yet. On those, and for anyone who prefers it, the Nix route stays as it was: with Nix and flakes enabled, run a command straight from the release.

other-platforms-and-the-nix-route.name: docs-install/other-platforms-and-the-nix-route-02
other-platforms-and-the-nix-route.text: Both print the same release and commit line as the bundle's commands do.

other-platforms-and-the-nix-route.name: docs-install/other-platforms-and-the-nix-route-03
other-platforms-and-the-nix-route.text: To check a release end to end, including the commands built from its archive, follow Download and verify a release. That verifier also checks each bundle against the commit the release tag names.

what-is-inside-the-tarball.name: docs-install/what-is-inside-the-tarball-01
what-is-inside-the-tarball.text: The folder bin holds the commands you run: singular, open-datum, devnet and cardano-node. Each is a short launcher that points the real program at the libraries and data files in the same folder and starts it, so nothing is read from outside the folder, and moving the folder moves the installation.

what-is-inside-the-tarball.name: docs-install/what-is-inside-the-tarball-02
what-is-inside-the-tarball.text: The folder share also holds the deployment blueprint, plutus.json, that the commands take as --blueprint, with version.txt beside it naming the release: singular registry describe reads its version label from that file and refuses a blueprint without one.

what-is-inside-the-tarball.name: docs-install/what-is-inside-the-tarball-03
what-is-inside-the-tarball.text: On Linux the folders lib and lib-node each also hold a C library and its loader, and the launcher starts the program through that loader, which is why the programs do not depend on the distribution's libraries. The Cardano node is built against another C library than the other three programs, which is why it has a folder of its own. On macOS the programs load only the libraries macOS itself provides and the ones in lib and lib-node.

what-you-download.name: docs-install/what-you-download-01
what-you-download.text: Every release after 0.12.0 carries one tarball per platform beside the documentation and on-chain archives, and one SHA256SUMS that lists all of them. A tarball holds both commands, singular and open-datum, with every library and data file they need. The tarballs of the releases after 0.13.1 also hold devnet, the program that starts a private development node, the Cardano node 10.7.0 it starts and the genesis files that node reads.

what-you-download.name: docs-install/what-you-download-02
what-you-download.text: The releases after 0.13.1 also carry the Linux packages, with their own checksum file singular-X.Y.Z-x86_64-linux.SHA256SUMS, and a Homebrew formula for the Mac. The sizes are approximate.

what-you-download.name: docs-install/what-you-download-03
what-you-download.text: Replace X.Y.Z with the release you want. The releases are listed at https://github.com/lambdasistemi/singular/releases.

what-you-see-when-it-works.name: docs-install/what-you-see-when-it-works-00
what-you-see-when-it-works.text: What you see when it works.

what-you-see-when-it-works.name: docs-install/what-you-see-when-it-works-01
what-you-see-when-it-works.text: Each command prints its name, the release and the commit it was built from, and exits with status 0. The commit is the one the release's tag names.

what-you-see-when-it-works.name: docs-install/what-you-see-when-it-works-02
what-you-see-when-it-works.text: The wallet commands run offline, so they are the quickest check that the programs work on your machine. Choose a passphrase; the program reads it from the standard input here and never takes it as an argument.

what-you-see-when-it-works.name: docs-install/what-you-see-when-it-works-03
what-you-see-when-it-works.text: Both commands print the same address, which begins with addr_test1 on the preprod network. From here the commands are the ones of the first demo.

what-you-see-when-it-works.name: docs-install/what-you-see-when-it-works-04
what-you-see-when-it-works.text: The development node starts with devnet and prints one line of settings once its chain is up. It runs until you stop it, and stopping devnet stops the Cardano node it started.

what-you-see-when-it-works.name: docs-install/what-you-see-when-it-works-05
what-you-see-when-it-works.text: The line is a JSON document that names the node's providerUrl and networkMagic, which is 42. The Demo 1 runbook in the singular-demo repository funds wallets on such a node and plays the whole demo. The node keeps its files in one folder under your temporary directory, so run one development node at a time.

where-the-blueprint-is.name: docs-install/where-the-blueprint-is-01
where-the-blueprint-is.text: Homebrew, the DEB, the RPM and the tarballs of a release after 0.13.1 bring the deployment blueprint the commands were released with, so Demo 1 needs no second download. It is the same file the on-chain archive ships as onchain/plutus.json, and verify-release checks that the two are identical. Each copy has the release's version.txt beside it.

where-the-blueprint-is.name: docs-install/where-the-blueprint-is-02
where-the-blueprint-is.text: Name it once and pass it to every command, for example blueprint=/usr/share/singular/plutus.json and then --blueprint "$blueprint".

how-to-change-effect-code.name: docs-io-ownership/how-to-change-effect-code-01
how-to-change-effect-code.text: Write the owner, lifetime and reason beside the implementation, not only in the allowlist.

how-to-change-effect-code.name: docs-io-ownership/how-to-change-effect-code-02
how-to-change-effect-code.text: Regenerate the site binding from the tree and review its diff beside the code change; commit both together.

how-to-change-effect-code.name: docs-io-ownership/how-to-change-effect-code-03
how-to-change-effect-code.text: Run the ownership check and its controls; hosted CI repeats them at the candidate head.

how-to-change-effect-code.name: docs-io-ownership/how-to-change-effect-code-04
how-to-change-effect-code.text: A change touching the session, receipt or reconcile modules beyond comments needs the stacked follow-on lane's attention first; ask before growing there.

the-story-this-serves.name: docs-io-ownership/the-story-this-serves-00
the-story-this-serves.text: The story this serves.

the-story-this-serves.name: docs-io-ownership/the-story-this-serves-01
the-story-this-serves.text: As a contributor, I add a counter to a command, a retry loop to a client or a coordination flag to a test, and the ownership check tells me exactly which file to classify it in, what to write beside it and what happens if I do not — before the review starts.

the-story-this-serves.name: docs-io-ownership/the-story-this-serves-02
the-story-this-serves.text: As a reviewer, I open this page and can tell which effects are necessary, who owns them, how long they live and which conformance-state work is still unfulfilled — without reading four hundred modules.

the-story-this-serves.name: docs-io-ownership/the-story-this-serves-03
the-story-this-serves.text: As an integrator, I learn that the product is single-threaded unless a written reason says otherwise, that no thread outlives its command, and that the unsafe escape hatch is absent from the tree — each with the check that would catch a regression.

what-backs-the-predecessors-and-what-sta.name: docs-io-ownership/what-backs-the-predecessors-and-what-stays-open-00
what-backs-the-predecessors-and-what-sta.text: What backs the predecessors, and what stays open.

what-backs-the-predecessors-and-what-sta.name: docs-io-ownership/what-backs-the-predecessors-and-what-stays-open-01
what-backs-the-predecessors-and-what-sta.text: Each row names the accepted evidence or the explicitly open requirement. Local paths are never public evidence; the hosted records below are.

what-the-census-covers.name: docs-io-ownership/what-the-census-covers-01
what-the-census-covers.text: The census discovers every Haskell source by walking the tree — no per-file list — and puts each in exactly one structural category. Anything it cannot classify fails the run instead of slipping through.

what-the-census-covers.name: docs-io-ownership/what-the-census-covers-02
what-the-census-covers.text: 455 sources in total. The census establishes structural facts — which files can name which effects — and never runtime behavior. That a module can name a mutable cell says nothing about what it does with it; what a command does is settled by the cage tests, the journeys and the hosted runs below, not here.

where-the-production-effects-live.name: docs-io-ownership/where-the-production-effects-live-01
where-the-production-effects-live.text: Every production effect below is allowlisted with the prose beside its implementation. The allowlist is the machine register; this table is the reader's summary.

where-the-production-effects-live.name: docs-io-ownership/where-the-production-effects-live-02
where-the-production-effects-live.text: The two trie adapters used to read as mutable state smuggled into pure computations. They are compatibility adapters with named callers and no locking: sharing one across threads without external serialization is a defect, and the haddock above each constructor says so.

which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-r.name: docs-io-ownership/which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-recorded-00
which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-r.text: Which effects are gated, and which only recorded.

which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-r.name: docs-io-ownership/which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-recorded-01
which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-r.text: A gated effect needs a file-level entry in the ownership allowlist naming its owner, lifetime, access model and reason. A new file naming one without an entry fails; an entry whose effect is gone fails as stale.

which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-r.name: docs-io-ownership/which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-recorded-02
which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-r.text: Three rows deserve emphasis. No module imports the unsafe IO library, so no unsafe escape exists in the tree; the control that plants one proves the check rejects it. No module calls forkIO; the product's only concurrency is the Async library's scoped combinators. No module uses STM; the one match for the word is a theorem name, not a transaction, which is why the STM class is import-anchored rather than token-anchored.

which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-r.name: docs-io-ownership/which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-recorded-03
which-effects-are-gated-and-which-only-r.text: Two further surfaces are recorded by the census but enforced elsewhere. Timeout bounds belong to the calling-thread confirmation design, whose deadline tests own them. Environment reads belong to the explicit-input rule, whose release-build exclusion the release controls own. Their carriers are named in the evidence map below.

which-way-dependencies-run.name: docs-io-ownership/which-way-dependencies-run-01
which-way-dependencies-run.text: Effects flow one way: libraries expose capabilities, commands and runners compose them, tests drive them. Five boundaries hold this shape over the discovered extent — namespaces, not file lists, so a moved module is rechecked with nothing to edit:

which-way-dependencies-run.name: docs-io-ownership/which-way-dependencies-run-02
which-way-dependencies-run.text: the conformance library never imports the runner (the library stays runnable without live effects);

which-way-dependencies-run.name: docs-io-ownership/which-way-dependencies-run-03
which-way-dependencies-run.text: the offchain libraries never import the command layer (commands consume the libraries, never the reverse);

which-way-dependencies-run.name: docs-io-ownership/which-way-dependencies-run-04
which-way-dependencies-run.text: each journey executable keeps its local modules (old runners are never extended by sharing);

which-way-dependencies-run.name: docs-io-ownership/which-way-dependencies-run-05
which-way-dependencies-run.text: no ordinary executable links a host module (the adversary stays outside the release, its test-only reader excepted);

which-way-dependencies-run.name: docs-io-ownership/which-way-dependencies-run-06
which-way-dependencies-run.text: the command layer is imported only at composition — commands, applications and tests.

who-owns-an-effect.name: docs-io-ownership/who-owns-an-effect-01
who-owns-an-effect.text: A contributor adding a mutable cell, a worker thread or an environment read wants to know where it belongs, who releases it and what check will ask about it. A reviewer wants to see each effect's owner, lifetime and reason in one place instead of reconstructing them from imports. This page is that map: what the census covers, which effects are allowed where, which way the module boundaries run, what evidence backs each predecessor ticket, and what stays openly unfulfilled.

why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.name: docs-io-ownership/why-the-product-stays-single-threaded-01
why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.text: The product runs on the calling thread unless a written, compelling reason says otherwise, and no thread outlives the command that started it. Four sites carry such reasons, each beside its implementation with its join:

why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.name: docs-io-ownership/why-the-product-stays-single-threaded-02
why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.text: The devnet probe runs a node and a client together, joined before the probe returns.

why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.name: docs-io-ownership/why-the-product-stays-single-threaded-03
why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.text: The private facade serves sessions beside their followers, each session cancelling and joining its children before the next starts.

why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.name: docs-io-ownership/why-the-product-stays-single-threaded-04
why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.text: The conformance node runner holds one node-to-client thread per session, joined before the session ends.

why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.name: docs-io-ownership/why-the-product-stays-single-threaded-05
why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.text: The CLI-backend control bounds one confirmation wait with an explicit cancel, observed and joined before the run ends.

why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.name: docs-io-ownership/why-the-product-stays-single-threaded-06
why-the-product-stays-single-threaded.text: The test parallelism (two mapConcurrently_ shards over independent examples) and the test coordinations (entered/released/hold flags joined by withAsync before each example ends) are harness-owned: they run only under the suites, never in a release build. A newly introduced forkIO, async or concurrently site in a product package fails the ownership check until it is classified with its reason and its join.

application-evolution-keep-the-same-repr.name: docs-lifecycle/application-evolution-keep-the-same-representative-00
application-evolution-keep-the-same-repr.text: Application evolution: keep the same representative.

application-evolution-keep-the-same-repr.name: docs-lifecycle/application-evolution-keep-the-same-representative-01
application-evolution-keep-the-same-repr.text: While the NFT is in application custody, the application spending validator governs its movement and state changes. An application update can spend one application UTxO and produce its successor with the same NFT. This need not change the registry.

application-evolution-keep-the-same-repr.name: docs-lifecycle/application-evolution-keep-the-same-representative-02
application-evolution-keep-the-same-repr.text: The application can observe its own inputs and transaction context. Avoiding observation of the mutable registry UTxO does not prohibit those checks or the use of authenticated registry configuration.

insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.name: docs-lifecycle/insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-folded-00
insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.text: Insert: certify first, check absence when folded.

insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.name: docs-lifecycle/insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-folded-01
insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.text: The application prepares a proposal identifying the registry, key, initial application state and destination application script/address. The configured application policy approves that exact proposal. The application minting policy must establish approval and enforce the required request format, binding and custody in that minting transaction. A correctly formatted Insert without accepted application approval is invalid; it cannot be used to register an arbitrary non-application datum. The application constructs the transaction. Its configured policy mints the Insert action token directly. When consuming the request, Singular recomputes the expected asset name from the Insert tag and necessary proposal parameters and recognizes it under that policy ID. No second mandatory native request policy/token is introduced.

insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.name: docs-lifecycle/insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-folded-02
insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.text: The pending Insert request contains its Insert action token but no representative NFT. Request creation need not observe the mutable registry state. Certification approves the proposed creation, not a claim that the key will remain absent.

insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.name: docs-lifecycle/insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-folded-03
insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.text: When folded successfully, Insert checks that the key is absent, changes it to Active, and mints its representative NFT into the output required by the certified proposal. The native checks must match that output's NFT, destination and initial state to the request. These effects occur together in the folding transaction.

insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.name: docs-lifecycle/insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-folded-04
insert-certify-first-check-absence-when-.text: Two Insert requests can target the same key while pending. An Insert whose key is occupied cannot succeed at that point. The design does not yet select whether a batch builder omits such requests or how failure is presented; it does not assume a skip rule inside the validator.

mint-move-and-burn.name: docs-lifecycle/mint-move-and-burn-01
mint-move-and-burn.text: The Insert/Withdraw action token certifies the exact action under the configured application policy. The representative NFT carries the identity's unique authority. They are not the same asset.

requests-folding-and-nft-custody.name: docs-lifecycle/requests-folding-and-nft-custody-01
requests-folding-and-nft-custody.text: Historical design. This page records the earlier Insert/Update/Delete design and its broader broader model successor. The active permanent permanent contract model supports only insertActive and updateTerminal. Historical tags 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 encode refused actions, not available features. Current supported behavior describes permanent contract; archived source and evidence remain on preserve/m2/pre-m1-source-removal.

requests-folding-and-nft-custody.name: docs-lifecycle/requests-folding-and-nft-custody-02
requests-folding-and-nft-custody.text: Request creation and folding are separate transactions. Each has its own atomic effects; there is an explicit pending interval between them. Creating a valid request does not guarantee that someone will fold it.

update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.name: docs-lifecycle/update-and-delete-transfer-authority-into-a-pending-request-00
update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.text: Update and Delete: transfer authority into a pending request.

update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.name: docs-lifecycle/update-and-delete-transfer-authority-into-a-pending-request-01
update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.text: To request retirement or removal, the application constructs a transaction that spends its NFT UTxO and places the existing representative into the Singular request output. Any additional Update/Delete request token and its issuer remain a construction detail; the existing NFT and exact authorized request binding are the adopted authority path.

update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.name: docs-lifecycle/update-and-delete-transfer-authority-into-a-pending-request-02
update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.text: The application validator must authorize that exact release: the chosen Update or Delete operation, registry/key binding and request destination. Merely being able to spend the NFT does not establish authorization for every operation. The releasing application validator enforces the request format, binding and custody at creation. Singular checks the native conditions at consumption; receiving the output alone does not execute Singular. No second application attestation token is required merely to repeat the approved release.

update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.name: docs-lifecycle/update-and-delete-transfer-authority-into-a-pending-request-03
update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.text: These checks need no observation of the mutable registry state when the request is created. The registry remains Active during the pending interval, and the NFT remains outstanding in the request. It cannot continue rotating as an application UTxO while held there.

update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.name: docs-lifecycle/update-and-delete-transfer-authority-into-a-pending-request-04
update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.text: Update/Delete requests are completion-only. There is no ordinary withdrawal, rejection or sweep that releases their representative. Valid folding consumes the request, burns the representative and applies exactly one of these transitions:

update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.name: docs-lifecycle/update-and-delete-transfer-authority-into-a-pending-request-05
update-and-delete-transfer-authority-int.text: The representative stays in request custody until that completion. Exact request-token disposal is still to be specified; it must not allow a completed request to be accepted again.

what-batching-establishes.name: docs-lifecycle/what-batching-establishes-01
what-batching-establishes.text: A fold traverses requests and applies their operations to the successive authenticated map states. Insert absence and Update/Delete old-value checks belong to those native mechanics. Certification and request recognition aim to keep the fold's own checks to explicit native obligations. A nonzero net burn of an application action token during folding still invokes its minting policy; whether that branch repeats expensive checks depends on the disposal contract. This is a design objective, not a measured performance result or a guarantee that every application fits.

what-batching-establishes.name: docs-lifecycle/what-batching-establishes-02
what-batching-establishes.text: One authentic representative cannot be held in two simultaneously pending Update/Delete requests for the same key. Consuming a request UTxO prevents consuming that UTxO again. These facts do not settle authorization replay across Delete followed by a fresh Insert, or all possible conflicts between different keys.

what-batching-establishes.name: docs-lifecycle/what-batching-establishes-03
what-batching-establishes.text: See certification and the remaining decisions.

where-the-representative-is-at-every-mom.name: docs-lifecycle/where-the-representative-is-at-every-moment-00
where-the-representative-is-at-every-mom.text: Where the representative is at every moment.

where-the-representative-is-at-every-mom.name: docs-lifecycle/where-the-representative-is-at-every-moment-01
where-the-representative-is-at-every-mom.text: A pending Insert holds no NFT; a pending Update or Delete holds the only one there is. Nothing but a valid fold moves the representative out of a terminal request.

withdrawing-a-pending-insert.name: docs-lifecycle/withdrawing-a-pending-insert-01
withdrawing-a-pending-insert.text: An Insert can be withdrawn without changing the registry or creating a representative. The configured application policy must approve a separate Withdraw action token whose asset name commits to the Withdraw tag, registry, exact pending Insert UTxO and required refund terms/effects. Singular checks that action binding when consuming the pending Insert. Original Insert approval alone cannot authorize cancellation.

withdrawing-a-pending-insert.name: docs-lifecycle/withdrawing-a-pending-insert-02
withdrawing-a-pending-insert.text: Token disposal, refund economics and the application's conditions for approving withdrawal remain to be specified. They must protect deposits and avoid assuming arbitrary outsiders may repeatedly cancel valid registration attempts.

archived-broader-model-evidence.name: docs-model-ledger/archived-broader-model-evidence-01
archived-broader-model-evidence.text: As a reviewer deciding how far to trust this model, use this page to see what it covers, what it deliberately abstracts, and — because this revision replaced the model wholesale — what happened to every guarantee the previous one made.

archived-broader-model-evidence.name: docs-model-ledger/archived-broader-model-evidence-02
archived-broader-model-evidence.text: This is a candidate at model-and-proofs stage. The executable machine is Singular.step in the model source. Every declaration is proved from the standard axioms; there is no audit verdict and no acceptance claim here.

model-ledger.name: docs-model-ledger/model-ledger-01
model-ledger.text: As a reader of current permanent contract, I can register a fresh key and terminate it permanently. The active model and compiled state support exactly tags 1 (insertActive) and 3 (updateTerminal); tags 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are explicitly refused, including caller-constructed and mixed requests. Application payload maintenance is separate. Current sources and receipts must be bound to the revised candidate.

model-ledger.name: docs-model-ledger/model-ledger-02
model-ledger.text: The detailed walkthrough and measurements below are archived broader model evidence, retained to explain the earlier contract; their broader success claims do not apply to permanent contract. Historical sources are retained on preserve/m2/pre-m1-source-removal. The active theorem manifest and the exact scope-retirement record explain the changed law and denominator. Unmet consumer requirements stay uncovered.

retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins.name: docs-model-ledger/retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins-00
retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins.text: Retired with the unused policy pins.

retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins.name: docs-model-ledger/retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins-01
retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins.text: Milestone one mints no absent or terminal token, so the registry state no longer pins a policy for either, and the model keeps one token kind. Four statements whose only subject was a token of a removed kind are retired with no replacement, and one is restated over the leaf:

retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins.name: docs-model-ledger/retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins-02
retired-with-the-unused-policy-pins.text: The lifecycle row that substituted a terminal policy at initialization is retired with the field it altered. The coverage record names every identity that changed.

the-retirement-map.name: docs-model-ledger/the-retirement-map-01
the-retirement-map.text: The previous model had 44 generic declarations. Registry mode replaced the alphabet, so most of them no longer have a subject. Every one is accounted for here — 1 carried, 3 renamed, 40 retired — because without this an auditor cannot tell a dropped guarantee from a rename, and a manifest that quietly lost rows would still satisfy every count.

the-retirement-map.name: docs-model-ledger/the-retirement-map-02
the-retirement-map.text: The registry-mode statements that replace them are listed in the theorem manifest.

what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.name: docs-model-ledger/what-is-covered-and-what-is-not-00
what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.text: What is covered, and what is not.

what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.name: docs-model-ledger/what-is-covered-and-what-is-not-01
what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.text: Covered: the seven edges and their deltas; the complement of the edge table as refusals with distinct reasons; admission by an approval scoped to the request's tuple; the leaf codec both ways; the fold's atomicity, zero-request refusal and mint check; the deposit's destination; and the seven promises over states reachable from genesis.

what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.name: docs-model-ledger/what-is-covered-and-what-is-not-02
what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.text: Not covered, and named rather than left to be discovered:

what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.name: docs-model-ledger/what-is-covered-and-what-is-not-03
what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.text: On-chain conformance. Nothing here says the cage validator implements this model. Whether the deployed validators do is the subject of the conformance evidence, not of this ledger.

what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.name: docs-model-ledger/what-is-covered-and-what-is-not-04
what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.text: The simulator. It replays 38 registry rows, 24 naming rows and 21 lifecycle rows and reproduces each verdict, and a mirror check binds the Lean it ships to the Lean it was built from. That is agreement on the exported inputs, not equivalence — and the transcriber is the model's author, so it is not an independent measurement either.

what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.name: docs-model-ledger/what-is-covered-and-what-is-not-05
what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.text: Plurality from genesis. terminal-witnesses-plural states that from any reachable terminal state arbitrarily many attestations can be minted. It does not construct a terminal key with zero attestations from genesis; that is a reachability claim about a fresh key and is not proved here.

what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.name: docs-model-ledger/what-is-covered-and-what-is-not-06
what-is-covered-and-what-is-not.text: Quantitative mutation coverage. Four mutants are executed (the mutation ledger); there is no survivor census.

what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts.name: docs-model-ledger/what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts-00
what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts.text: What the model is, and what it abstracts.

what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts.name: docs-model-ledger/what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts-01
what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts.text: The trie answers two questions and nothing else: is this key known, and where in its life is it. Applications store nothing in the leaf. Seven edges move a leaf, each an MPFS primitive applied to a state, each a delta over the one token kind a fold mints, the active witness.

what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts.name: docs-model-ledger/what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts-02
what-the-model-is-and-what-it-abstracts.text: Deliberate abstractions, each of which a reader should hold against every claim below:

archived-broader-model-evidence.name: docs-mutants/archived-broader-model-evidence-01
archived-broader-model-evidence.text: As someone deciding whether to trust these proofs, use this register to see that the model's guarantees actually constrain the model — that each law was shown to fail when the behaviour it describes is broken, rather than merely shown to compile when it is not.

archived-broader-model-evidence.name: docs-mutants/archived-broader-model-evidence-02
archived-broader-model-evidence.text: The four mutations below are the ones the registry-mode epic names. Each was executed. None is a proposal.

limits.name: docs-mutants/limits-01
limits.text: Four mutants are four points, not a mutation score. A campaign that enumerated every guard and reported a survivor census would say more, and is not what this is: these four were chosen because the interface names them as the failures its witness laws exist to prevent.

limits.name: docs-mutants/limits-02
limits.text: A killed mutant shows the proofs constrain the mutated definition. It does not show the definition is the right one — that is what the operator's rulings, the interface and the simulation are for.

mutation-ledger.name: docs-mutants/mutation-ledger-01
mutation-ledger.text: As a reader of current permanent contract, I can register a fresh key and terminate it permanently. The active model and compiled state support exactly tags 1 (insertActive) and 3 (updateTerminal); tags 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are explicitly refused, including caller-constructed and mixed requests. Application payload maintenance is separate. Current sources and receipts must be bound to the revised candidate.

mutation-ledger.name: docs-mutants/mutation-ledger-02
mutation-ledger.text: The detailed walkthrough and measurements below are archived broader model evidence, retained to explain the earlier contract; their broader success claims do not apply to permanent contract. Historical sources are retained on preserve/m2/pre-m1-source-removal. The active theorem manifest and the exact scope-retirement record explain the changed law and denominator. Unmet consumer requirements stay uncovered.

the-mutants.name: docs-mutants/the-mutants-01
the-mutants.text: Positive control: on the unmutated tree the statements prove, and the compiled axiom report carries no sorryAx.

what-counts-as-a-kill-here.name: docs-mutants/what-counts-as-a-kill-here-00
what-counts-as-a-kill-here.text: What counts as a kill here.

what-counts-as-a-kill-here.name: docs-mutants/what-counts-as-a-kill-here-01
what-counts-as-a-kill-here.text: A mutant is killed when a named obligation stops holding, not when the file stops compiling. Those are different events and only the first is evidence:

what-counts-as-a-kill-here.name: docs-mutants/what-counts-as-a-kill-here-02
what-counts-as-a-kill-here.text: the mutated definition must elaborate first, so what is measured is a semantic change and not a syntax error;

what-counts-as-a-kill-here.name: docs-mutants/what-counts-as-a-kill-here-03
what-counts-as-a-kill-here.text: the kill must land on an obligation, not on a restatement. Mutating applyEdge trivially breaks the effect lemmas that restate applyEdge, which proves nothing; so each mutation carries its effect lemma with it, and the failure surfaces where the invariant is established;

what-counts-as-a-kill-here.name: docs-mutants/what-counts-as-a-kill-here-04
what-counts-as-a-kill-here.text: a positive control shows the same obligations hold on the unmutated tree.

what-counts-as-a-kill-here.name: docs-mutants/what-counts-as-a-kill-here-05
what-counts-as-a-kill-here.text: The first run of this campaign killed all four at the effect lemmas. That was a near-tautological result and was discarded rather than reported.

what-counts-as-a-kill-here.name: docs-mutants/what-counts-as-a-kill-here-06
what-counts-as-a-kill-here.text: The campaign mutated Model.lean at sha256 c951e4bd7a0037431238affac3e85aa07f3c505d1a7fde4b15c9d86df7669cc8. The current Model.lean is beec6567f46b7b0bb273ebe3e28cf7197bf56668bcdf8dfd4590c58ec6d29d97, and the campaign has not been rerun against it: the four rows below are evidence about the revision they name and nothing later. The absent and terminal token kinds have since left the model, so three of the four mutations (those that mint an absent token, attest a key, or keep a custody entry) cannot be written against it; the rows stand as history. A campaign is evidence about the exact definitions it broke, so a later model is a later campaign, not a carried-forward result.

why-the-kills-land-where-they-do.name: docs-mutants/why-the-kills-land-where-they-do-00
why-the-kills-land-where-they-do.text: Why the kills land where they do.

why-the-kills-land-where-they-do.name: docs-mutants/why-the-kills-land-where-they-do-01
why-the-kills-land-where-they-do.text: Every promise in the interface is read off one invariant — Consistent — which step_ok_consistent proves survives each of the seven edges. active-witness-unique and absent-witness-unique are its supply conjuncts read one state at a time, supply-matches-leaf-state is the same fact stated as a biconditional, witness-kinds-exclude follows from the supply conjuncts plus a key having one leaf, and terminal-attestation-sound is its terminal-holding conjunct. So a mutation that breaks a supply law breaks the invariant's corresponding conjunct, and everything downstream of it fails with it.

why-the-kills-land-where-they-do.name: docs-mutants/why-the-kills-land-where-they-do-02
why-the-kills-land-where-they-do.text: attest-active-key is the one worth reading closely. Dropping the terminal requirement from the read does not break arithmetic; it breaks a derivation. The witnessTerminal branch establishes that the attested key's leaf is terminal by reading it out of the verified read. With the mutation the read no longer carries that fact, so the attestation can no longer be shown sound — which is exactly terminal-attestation-sound failing, and exactly the defect the mutation describes.

finding-alice.name: docs-naming-demo/finding-alice-01
finding-alice.text: The asset name IS the registry key. Given the registry's active policy id, alice's witness is that policy plus the raw bytes of alice — no hash, no controller, no registry token, no prefix and no incarnation enters it:

finding-alice.name: docs-naming-demo/finding-alice-02
finding-alice.text: That is the naming partition's convention, where the witness policies are the absent, active and terminal policies. The registry partition deployed on preprod names its representative differently: by the BLAKE2b-256 digest of the spelling under the representative policy, as the preprod record shows. The two queries are not interchangeable; each finds a token only under its own partition's policies.

finding-alice.name: docs-naming-demo/finding-alice-03
finding-alice.text: The following Koios queries are a historical diagnostic for the earlier preprod naming walkthrough. The dated naming and escrow plays require an indexed read path with a recorded chain point and freshness; registry follower #107 tracks that path. A Koios response alone does not satisfy those plays.

finding-alice.name: docs-naming-demo/finding-alice-04
finding-alice.text: For that historical query, substitute the published active policy id and use Koios Asset UTxOs:

finding-alice.name: docs-naming-demo/finding-alice-05
finding-alice.text: The holding address and inline datum identify the live record or the completion-only custody a pending ending put it in. No trie lookup and no creation-controller lookup is needed to locate a live witness.

finding-alice.name: docs-naming-demo/finding-alice-06
finding-alice.text: The three policies share that one convention, so the same query answers three different questions about the same name. A witness under the absent policy says somebody has staked a deposit on the name being free. A witness under the active policy says the name is booked, and its holding output is the record. A witness under the terminal policy says the name is over — anyone may ask for one by folding a read, and nobody can ever make the name live again.

finding-alice.name: docs-naming-demo/finding-alice-07
finding-alice.text: The token's presence at a live output is the witness being read; this example does not query the root or walk history. A connected demonstration also records which indexed chain state supplied that output.

fixture-fields-and-finite-model-limits.name: docs-naming-demo/fixture-fields-and-finite-model-limits-01
fixture-fields-and-finite-model-limits.text: Values are finite-model fixtures, not product or economic policy: the profile fixes where a deposit returns and invents no fee, bond, price, expiry, deposit-amount or refund-value rule. alice maps to one frozen demo key. The request stores a refund address inside its Insert commitment, and cancellation can only copy that address. Continue to the lifecycle page for destination maintenance, committed-controller recovery, and split retirement through either the controller or published quorum. Retirement-request withdrawal is a distinct refusal case. The naming proposal's generic output payload stays the generic demo constants; fixtures are first-class fields beside it, never packed into it.

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-00
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: How a name moves in the registry.

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-01
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: Naming is an instance of the registry, not a layer bolted beside it. A name is one key in the registry's authenticated map, and the value of that key is a single byte:

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-02
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: Seven requests move a key, and nothing else does. Each one moves a witness token, and the witness is what a reader looks at — never the root:

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-03
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: Every other shape is refused before any proof is checked, and each refusal carries one trace label naming its own reason.

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-05
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: A witness moves only inside a fold. A mint or a burn under the absent, active or terminal policy is accepted only in a transaction that spends the registry's state token and folds it.

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-06
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: The fold decides how many, and where. It sums the witness column of the requests it consumed, and the transaction's mint under the three policies must equal that sum exactly — asset by asset, quantity by quantity. Nothing else may move under them.

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-07
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: A terminal witness is its holder's to destroy. It says a name is over, forever; burning your own copy costs the registry nothing, so that burn alone needs no fold.

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-08
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: The asset name is the registry key. Identity is the pair of policy and key, so a name recreated after a delete carries the same identity again.

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-09
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: One edge carries a rule of its own: ending a name needs the committed recovery key or the retirement quorum, and never the current control key alone.

how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.name: docs-naming-demo/how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry-10
how-a-name-moves-in-the-registry.text: No application script at fold time. The naming validator is not executed by a fold at all. What it does instead is certify an edge in advance: it mints one approval whose asset name binds the edge, the key, the owner and the destination, the requester attaches that approval to their request, and the cage recomputes the name from the request itself and refuses anything that does not match. A folder is permissionless and can therefore be anyone, which is exactly why the destination is bound: without it a folder could route your name to itself.

how-the-pieces-relate.name: docs-naming-demo/how-the-pieces-relate-01
how-the-pieces-relate.text: Naming does not re-implement the registry and the page does not re-implement naming. The previous simulator did re-implement it, in about nine hundred lines of JavaScript, and when the Lean moved those lines went on describing a model that no longer existed while still reporting green. What the page transcribes is the replay: every row is a verdict the Lean computed, and the page recomputes or re-checks it in front of you.

naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it.name: docs-naming-demo/naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it-00
naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it.text: Naming: book a name, retire it, attest it.

naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it.name: docs-naming-demo/naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it-01
naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it.text: As a reader of current permanent contract, I can register a fresh key and terminate it permanently. The active model and compiled state support exactly tags 1 (insertActive) and 3 (updateTerminal); tags 0, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are explicitly refused, including caller-constructed and mixed requests. Application payload maintenance is separate. Current sources and receipts must be bound to the revised candidate.

naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it.name: docs-naming-demo/naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it-02
naming-book-a-name-retire-it-attest-it.text: The detailed walkthrough and measurements below are archived broader model evidence, retained to explain the earlier contract; their broader success claims do not apply to permanent contract. Historical sources are retained on preserve/m2/pre-m1-source-removal. The active theorem manifest and the exact scope-retirement record explain the changed law and denominator. Unmet consumer requirements stay uncovered.

status-of-this-candidate.name: docs-naming-demo/status-of-this-candidate-01
status-of-this-candidate.text: The naming profile is an unaccepted candidate: proven in Lean, replayed in the simulator, and playable in the browser. The Nix-built documentation archive packages its raw model, corpus, replay inputs, and exact identities for review; building that bundle is not release publication or on-chain acceptance. The live preview is bound to the pull-request head, and the served page states the candidate is unaccepted.

what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here.name: docs-naming-demo/what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here-00
what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here.text: What is proved and what is checked here.

what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here.name: docs-naming-demo/what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here-01
what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here.text: The naming instance carries seven theorem declarations, its lifecycle nine and its wire encoding five — twenty-one in all, each PROVED in Lean from the standard axioms alone and each in its own manifest with its own compiled gate, separate from the registry's forty-four. The theorem manifest derives these counts from the manifests rather than stating them by hand. The naming statements are stated as characterisations rather than one-way implications: the retirement rule says exactly when retirement is certified, so a model that certified more than the rule allows fails them as surely as one that certified less.

what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here.name: docs-naming-demo/what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here-02
what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here.text: The page replays twenty-four naming rows and twenty-one lifecycle rows, and requires the verdict it computes to be the verdict the Lean exported.

what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here.name: docs-naming-demo/what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here-03
what-is-proved-and-what-is-checked-here.text: Finite checks are finite: the corpus replays measure the transcription on its rows; they do not prove the quantified statements, and they do not make the candidate accepted.

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-00
what-you-can-do.text: What you can do.

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-01
what-you-can-do.text: Watch the journey. Five steps, played rather than asserted:

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-02
what-you-can-do.text: The controller books alice. One insertActive, certified by the controller's signature. The active token goes to the record.

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-03
what-you-can-do.text: A quorum retires it. One updateTerminal. The active token is burned and the leaf can never move again. The control key alone cannot do this — the rule is the committed recovery key revealed and signing, or a distinct-member quorum, and the control key on its own is neither.

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-04
what-you-can-do.text: A folded read mints the Over witness. witnessTerminal needs no approval at all: anyone may attest a retired name.

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-05
what-you-can-do.text: And another. The terminal witness is plural, because the attestation is a read. Both copies are true.

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-06
what-you-can-do.text: Burn them both. The leaf is still terminal. An attestation says something that stays true whether or not you keep the token.

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-07
what-you-can-do.text: Read the replay below it. Twenty-four naming rows across six sections — spellings, queues, folds, transitions, resolutions and replays — each one a verdict the Lean computed, recomputed in your browser. Two of them carry the amended retirement rule — the control key alone never retires, and the quorum does — and a third shows the other route, retirement by the recovery key.

what-you-can-do.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-can-do-08
what-you-can-do.text: Then the lifecycle. Twenty-one more rows: seeding the consumer with its pinned policies, moving a payment destination while the registry root stays put, revealing the committed recovery key, and both retirement routes with the refusals that guard them.

what-you-see-when-it-is-refused.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-see-when-it-is-refused-00
what-you-see-when-it-is-refused.text: What you see when it is refused.

what-you-see-when-it-is-refused.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-see-when-it-is-refused-01
what-you-see-when-it-is-refused.text: Every refusal names its intended condition. A generic exception is a defect.

what-you-see-when-it-is-refused.name: docs-naming-demo/what-you-see-when-it-is-refused-02
what-you-see-when-it-is-refused.text: The last two are the ones worth trying by hand in the generic profile's free play. The retirement row and the delete row are deliberately different names: naming defines no delete, and a retirement that met neither authorization route is a different failure that must not wear delete's name.

who-this-is-for.name: docs-naming-demo/who-this-is-for-00
who-this-is-for.text: Who this is for.

who-this-is-for.name: docs-naming-demo/who-this-is-for-01
who-this-is-for.text: A reviewer who wants to play the naming profile in the docs rather than read a proposed walkthrough. Naming is an instance of the registry, not a second model: the same seven edges, the same tokens, the same refusals, with naming's own rule about who may certify what.

who-this-is-for.name: docs-naming-demo/who-this-is-for-02
who-this-is-for.text: Open the simulator and switch the profile picker to Naming — the Over witness.

book-a-name.name: docs-naming-lifecycle/book-a-name-01
book-a-name.text: Alice signs the naming policy's approval mint for registration. Its asset name binds the key, owner and the application's destination address and datum hash. She places the approval and deposit in a registry request. Any folder can then fold it. The fold delivers the active witness and booked datum to the approved address. The registration deposit accompanies that carrier; it is not a separate refund to Alice. A wrong tuple, policy or quantity refuses.

change-the-payment-destination.name: docs-naming-lifecycle/change-the-payment-destination-01
change-the-payment-destination.text: The current controller may set, replace or clear one optional payment destination. Routing data need not belong to the controller. The successor preserves the registry identity, key, active witness, controller, next-control commitment and retirement quorum. Missing or wrong controller authorization, multiple destinations and altered control fields refuse.

consumer-and-ledger-boundary.name: docs-naming-lifecycle/consumer-and-ledger-boundary-01
consumer-and-ledger-boundary.text: The design-time consumer contract is bound to lambdasistemi/cardano-keri commit 14a64a4681d3e429fab5877062b5c476c2a4bfe2. It uses Conway inline-datum and required-signer precedents without importing KERI schemas or claiming compiled interoperability. Singular publishes its constructor indices and field order, binds one registry identity to an application and refuses a rival registry seed.

consumer-and-ledger-boundary.name: docs-naming-lifecycle/consumer-and-ledger-boundary-02
