When every transaction has landed, the command's fields are stated as fact. Otherwise they stay under expected. When the node refuses a transaction, the run ends as a ledger refusal, and wentThrough names the transactions that landed before it.

what-each-receipt-says.name: docs-singular-node/what-each-receipt-says-02
what-each-receipt-says.text: Signing elsewhere: the outcome waiting-for-signatures and the bundle. That is its hash, the written and the saved path, the signer, and per transaction its step, identity, deadline and effect lines. The command's own fields sit under expected, because nothing has landed yet.

what-each-receipt-says.name: docs-singular-node/what-each-receipt-says-03
what-each-receipt-says.text: A key file (being retired): the receipt it has always printed.

what-each-receipt-says.name: docs-singular-node/what-each-receipt-says-04
what-each-receipt-says.text: Status 19 also ends any write that a pending bundle stops before it builds anything. Its receipt names that bundle under pendingBundle: its hash, its saved path, and the transactions still awaited with their deadlines. Recovering a registry command follows a bundle from there.

what-each-receipt-says.name: docs-singular-node/what-each-receipt-says-05
what-each-receipt-says.text: A pending bundle stops the next write of the same registry by the same wallet only. A write in another registry, a create of a new registry included, is not stopped, and it may spend a wallet output that the pending bundle needs.

what-each-receipt-says.name: docs-singular-node/what-each-receipt-says-06
what-each-receipt-says.text: A bundle whose transactions carry a deadline then dies by expiry, and running the command again rebuilds it. A bundle signed elsewhere whose transactions carry none, an open-datum insert, update or terminate without --fold and a create, never expires: if it can never land, it keeps stopping the next write of that registry by that wallet at status 19. The way out today is, for a create, a create that names another output with --seed, as When a bundle waits for signatures says; for the others, --state-dir naming another state directory, which starts a fresh journal for that registry and wallet.

what-i-do-with-the-address.name: docs-singular-node/what-i-do-with-the-address-00
what-i-do-with-the-address.text: What I do with the address.

what-i-do-with-the-address.name: docs-singular-node/what-i-do-with-the-address-01
what-i-do-with-the-address.text: I keep the address with the registry's name, I send it to whoever should act on it, and I give it to --registry instead of the state token and the network. --save-state-token still keeps the state token in the settings file as the key state-token, and the commands after a create find it there as before. A registry named by the state token and the network works exactly as it did.

what-the-address-is.name: docs-singular-node/what-the-address-is-01
what-the-address-is.text: The address is the registry's NFT, the one asset that is the registry on chain, written as one bech32 word. The word has four parts, and its body is the state token and nothing else:

what-the-address-is.name: docs-singular-node/what-the-address-is-02
what-the-address-is.text: The body of the word is the 28 bytes of the policy followed by the 32 bytes of the name, which is exactly the state token that POLICY.NAME spells in hex; the address is that token with its network and a checksum. The checksum is the original bech32 one, and the word is printed in lower case. It is read in all lower case or all upper case, never in a mixture. The receipt of create prints the address as registry, the state token as stateToken, unchanged, and the CIP-14 fingerprint of the same asset as fingerprint: the short name that wallets and explorers show for it. On success one line on standard error says the three.

what-the-address-is.name: docs-singular-node/what-the-address-is-03
what-the-address-is.text: The prefix names the network. Four networks have one:

what-the-address-is.name: docs-singular-node/what-the-address-is-04
what-the-address-is.text: On any other network a create still works, prints null as registry, keeps the fingerprint and says on standard error that the network has no prefix. The address says which network to use, and nothing else about it: the Koios URL and the pinned time directory are still given, and the network the address names is the network every later step uses, exactly as --network-magic would be.

what-the-address-is.name: docs-singular-node/what-the-address-is-05
what-the-address-is.text: The address does not say what the registry is for. The blueprint does. singular registry describe --blueprint plutus.json --registry ADDRESS with a Koios URL prints the page, and its release section names the blueprint's title and the application script the registry pins, which is the application that decides what its keys hold. The same page and the receipt of inspect carry the address, the state token and the fingerprint of the registry they read.

when-the-provider-cannot-be-used.name: docs-singular-node/when-the-provider-cannot-be-used-00
when-the-provider-cannot-be-used.text: When the provider cannot be used.

area-vocabulary.name: docs-test-selection/area-vocabulary-01
area-vocabulary.text: All suites compile the same Area type in offchain/test-tags/Test/Tags.hs. Its constructors produce the following lowercase labels. Add a label only when a gate needs it, then document it here.

area-vocabulary.name: docs-test-selection/area-vocabulary-02
area-vocabulary.text: For example, network-time examples start under Singular.Registry.NetworkTime [time][provider]. A gate changing time material can select time; a broader adapter change can select provider. Module names omit a trailing Spec suffix.

checks-execute-unit-binaries.name: docs-test-selection/checks-execute-unit-binaries-01
checks-execute-unit-binaries.text: From offchain/, build the unit checks directly:

checks-execute-unit-binaries.name: docs-test-selection/checks-execute-unit-binaries-02
checks-execute-unit-binaries.text: From conformance/, nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.conformance-tests executes the Hspec appendix. Each check runs its existing app or binary during the Nix build, fails when that execution fails and retains the output at the check's store path. A cached result represents an earlier successful execution on the same inputs. The vector command generates vectors; it is not an Hspec suite. Record-value checks receive the naming validator blueprint compiled from the current source. Apps and supported package exports remain available.

checks-execute-unit-binaries.name: docs-test-selection/checks-execute-unit-binaries-03
checks-execute-unit-binaries.text: The development-node suites and the live conformance book stay executable apps. Compiling or listing their examples does not establish live ledger behavior. The inventory discovers the Hspec entrypoints from Cabal, rejects unwrapped spec calls and unknown tag constructors, and exercises removal and unknown-tag controls. It is a source inventory; compiled paths and before-and-after example counts supply the separate runtime evidence.

observed-selections.name: docs-test-selection/observed-selections-01
observed-selections.text: On 6 October 2026, the three selections above executed 69, 18 and 341 examples respectively, each with zero failures. Compare a future run's actual summary with this dated measurement; test additions can change the counts.

observed-selections.name: docs-test-selection/observed-selections-02
observed-selections.text: The full off-chain suite has 1,037 examples, the conformance appendix 573, the end-to-end suite 69, the contract suite 48 and the compiled record-value suite four. Tagging preserves their example counts. A dry run establishes the census of development-node examples, not execution of their scenarios.

select-an-area-or-module.name: docs-test-selection/select-an-area-or-module-01
select-an-area-or-module.text: Run the off-chain commands from offchain/. Keep the brackets quoted so the shell passes them literally to Hspec:

select-an-area-or-module.name: docs-test-selection/select-an-area-or-module-02
select-an-area-or-module.text: The time filter matches the literal tag wherever it occurs in a path. The module filter uses a leading slash for the path segment start and a trailing space for the end of the module name. The slash-terminated form selects nothing: Hspec matches substrings of the joined path, and the tags sit between the module name and the next slash. Combining match with skip first selects matching paths and then excludes the skipped paths. Different area tags on one module mean that either area can select its examples; they do not duplicate examples.

select-tests-for-the-code-you-change.name: docs-test-selection/select-tests-for-the-code-you-change-00
select-tests-for-the-code-you-change.text: Select tests for the code you change.

select-tests-for-the-code-you-change.name: docs-test-selection/select-tests-for-the-code-you-change-01
select-tests-for-the-code-you-change.text: As a contributor, you want to run the tests for the areas your change can affect and see exactly which examples you selected. Each Hspec path starts with a stable module name and bracketed area tags. Selecting an area includes every module carrying that tag; selecting a module narrows the run to that module. A filtered run proves only its selected examples. Pending examples remain unexecuted.

suite-commands-and-evidence-limits.name: docs-test-selection/suite-commands-and-evidence-limits-01
suite-commands-and-evidence-limits.text: The Cabal manifests declare five Hspec suites: cage-tests, e2e-tests exposed as cage-tests-e2e, contract-tests, record-value-tests, and conformance-tests exposed for filtering as conformance-appendix-tests. The record-value entrypoint defines its examples inline, under the module name Main. Contract checks include repeated runs of the same case list against different adapters, each wrapped under its defining module. Development-node evidence descriptions and conformance appendix markers remain inside the module groups.

suite-commands-and-evidence-limits.name: docs-test-selection/suite-commands-and-evidence-limits-02
suite-commands-and-evidence-limits.text: The public conformance command nix run .#conformance-tests, run from conformance/, executes the live product book as well as its appendix. Use nix run .#conformance-appendix-tests -- --match "[conformance]" to filter the Hspec appendix alone. The published book's requirement text and receipt-computed coverage are unchanged by these harness labels.

suite-commands-and-evidence-limits.name: docs-test-selection/suite-commands-and-evidence-limits-03
suite-commands-and-evidence-limits.text: The evaluation spike's cleanup-control uses Tasty, so it is outside this Hspec vocabulary. Naming's direct-GHC codec and drift programs are not Hspec suites either. The Cabal-declared Conformance.Support.Authenticate module was already absent from the Hspec entrypoint; it remains inactive so tagging changes neither suite membership nor example counts. No new exclusion is introduced.

exact-declaration-inventory.name: docs-theorems/exact-declaration-inventory-01
exact-declaration-inventory.text: The reference-read rejection statements concern accepted economic transactions and reachable worlds. They preserve the registry and its state and singular tokens, require actual state reference reads, protect live registrations and terminations, and preserve the inputs of a disjoint fold. Tag burns count policy/name quantities without a hash-injectivity premise. The retained legacy rejection statements describe the superseded state-spending path followed by the deployed validators; their proof status does not certify the reference-read rule. Economic rejection and retraction now enforce refund floors. Each refund address receives at least the sum owed by its distinct consumed requests: held lovelace minus the declared tip on rejection, and all held lovelace on retraction. Registration cost is included in both returns. Retraction requires the refund address signature, one pending registration, its whole reclaim interval, both tags burned, no state read or spend, and removal from the pool. All actual outputs at an address contribute, including payments for another purpose at that address. Economic folds now enforce observed model balance, exact donation and declared carrier routing, with ordinary funding paying the fee. Gross processor reward equals the consumed tips: ordinary outputs plus fee equal actual ordinary inputs plus tips. Output categories follow holdings, including when addresses coincide. A pending termination has an accepted model transaction at any time under explicit folder willingness, funding and fee hypotheses. This is not ledger inclusion or builder acceptance. Trie-ready tags in the world match pending requests; application tags held by pending registrations match those registrations, with one each. No total application-tag supply outside Singular, ledger minimum, fee market or flood price is proved. These statements carry no implementation or ledger acceptance.

exact-declaration-inventory.name: docs-theorems/exact-declaration-inventory-02
exact-declaration-inventory.text: The naming, lifecycle and wire declarations are listed in their own manifests: naming-theorem-debt.json, lifecycle-theorem-debt.json and wire-theorem-debt.json.

how-this-register-is-kept-honest.name: docs-theorems/how-this-register-is-kept-honest-00
how-this-register-is-kept-honest.text: How this register is kept honest.

how-this-register-is-kept-honest.name: docs-theorems/how-this-register-is-kept-honest-01
how-this-register-is-kept-honest.text: A compiled gate in Audit.lean runs while the library elaborates: it collects the axioms of every theorem in the frozen module and fails the build if any lies outside the three standard ones. Re-admitting a single theorem turns the build red, so a sorry cannot reach this page.

how-this-register-is-kept-honest.name: docs-theorems/how-this-register-is-kept-honest-02
how-this-register-is-kept-honest.text: tools/check_model.py then cross-checks three things that are easy to let drift apart: the source declarations against the manifests, the compiled axiom report against both, and — added after the drift below was found — this page against the manifest. The last one exists because it was missing: before it, the page claimed 41 declarations while the manifest held 44, and three proved statements appeared nowhere. The check is set equality, and the total above is derived from the manifest rather than typed by hand.

theorem-manifest.name: docs-theorems/theorem-manifest-01
theorem-manifest.text: As a proof reviewer, use this register to identify exactly which statements the registry-mode model supplies, that each one is proved, and from which axioms. Every declaration keeps its qualified name and a digest of its statement text, so a changed or missing obligation is detectable rather than merely unlikely.

theorem-manifest.name: docs-theorems/theorem-manifest-02
theorem-manifest.text: All 84 declarations of the registry's own statement module are PROVED from the standard axioms — propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound — and nothing else. The naming instance adds 7, its lifecycle 9 and its wire encoding 5, for 105 in total, each with its own manifest and its own compiled gate.

theorem-manifest.name: docs-theorems/theorem-manifest-03
theorem-manifest.text: The operator-authorized source removal retires ten declarations about excluded success behavior. Their historical proofs and receipts remain on preserve/m2/pre-m1-source-removal; they do not certify permanent contract. The active model retains the applicable invariant, exit, refund, datum and public-fold laws. Public unmet consumer requirements remain uncovered.

what-the-seven-promises-are.name: docs-theorems/what-the-seven-promises-are-01
what-the-seven-promises-are.text: The interface states seven guarantees the registry makes for every application, and the model proves each one over states reachable from genesis by folds. Reachability is a hypothesis, not a weakening: over an arbitrary State value the supply laws are simply false.

what-the-seven-promises-are.name: docs-theorems/what-the-seven-promises-are-02
what-the-seven-promises-are.text: Every promise is reached through one invariant — Consistent — that the model proves survives each supported transition. That is why the statements read as consequences rather than as separate arguments.

what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-n.name: docs-theorems/what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-not-00
what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-n.text: What this establishes, and what it does not.

what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-n.name: docs-theorems/what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-not-01
what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-n.text: These proofs establish properties of the model. They do not establish that the model is the right model, and no build ever will: that is what the operator's rulings, the interface and the simulation are for. A theorem can also be true and narrower than its name, so the column above says what each one states rather than leaving the name to imply it.

what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-n.name: docs-theorems/what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-not-02
what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-n.text: The model is abstract where the chain is concrete. Commitments stand for collision-free canonical commitments, the trie is a logical authenticated map, and an approval's asset name is a commitment over the tuple it scopes rather than a real BLAKE2b digest. The executable consumer supplies the real hashes; the model fixes the complete preimages.

what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-n.name: docs-theorems/what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-not-03
what-this-establishes-and-what-it-does-n.text: Retraction admission is stated over a finite validity interval. Its bounds are read off the request script's in_phase2 and the ledger's validity interval, whose lower bound is included and upper bound excluded. The model's bounds are finite, so an interval open at either end is not a case it can be asked: that is a named non-goal, not a gap waiting on a ticket, and the chain side is pinned by the request validator's Aiken exact-outcome tests — they admit an owner-signed retraction at the window's included lower bound and where its excluded upper bound reaches the retraction time's end, and refuse it with the named not-phase2 one unit before the lower bound and one unit past the upper, and for an interval with no lower or no upper bound alike. The finite cases are compared live: the retraction-window row (retract-outside-window) submits an owner-signed retraction before phase 2 and one after it on a devnet, both refused by the request script and answered not-phase2 by the model, which agrees on every step. The deployed validators are compiled without traces, so this run's live refusals expose no name: they are attributed to the applied request script, and the name itself is never described as a live observation (#287).

checking-files-you-already-have.name: docs-verify-release/checking-files-you-already-have-01
checking-files-you-already-have.text: If you downloaded the three assets yourself, point the verifier at their directory; every check after the download is the same:

checking-files-you-already-have.name: docs-verify-release/checking-files-you-already-have-02
checking-files-you-already-have.text: From v0.8.0 on, every release is verified this way by the release workflow itself, right after it is published.

download-and-verify-a-release.name: docs-verify-release/download-and-verify-a-release-01
download-and-verify-a-release.text: You have cloned nothing. You want to know that a Singular release is what it says it is before you run it: that the files you downloaded are the files that were published, that the release names the formal model its evidence was checked against, and that the singular and open-datum commands built from it actually run a registry from creation to termination. One command answers all three, from the downloaded bytes alone, and either passes or refuses by name.

what-a-refusal-means.name: docs-verify-release/what-a-refusal-means-01
what-a-refusal-means.text: A refusal is one line, verify-release: REFUSED <name>: <detail>, and the exit status is 1.

what-a-refusal-means.name: docs-verify-release/what-a-refusal-means-02
what-a-refusal-means.text: A release that passes prints its tag, both archive checksums, the model revision and the directory it was verified in.

what-it-checks-in-order.name: docs-verify-release/what-it-checks-in-order-01
what-it-checks-in-order.text: Each check runs only when the ones before it passed, and the first one that fails ends the run with one line naming why.

what-it-checks-in-order.name: docs-verify-release/what-it-checks-in-order-02
what-it-checks-in-order.text: The model revision is the commit of the application model, the formal specification the conformance evidence reads its statements at. The release states it in the archive as MODEL-REVISION; the verifier compares it with the revision the conformance evidence of the same release is compiled against. The journey is the one on the archive's run page: a registry is created, a key inserted, its payload updated and the key terminated, each a separate singular or open-datum process on one development network the verifier starts and stops itself, with an inspect after every write.

what-it-checks-in-order.name: docs-verify-release/what-it-checks-in-order-03
what-it-checks-in-order.text: Before starting the journey, the verifier strips and inspects the actual compiled singular and open-datum executables and reads their resolved registry CLI build flags. Both must exclude hidden test inputs and disable the test flag. It then records every ordinary journey invocation: all five commands must run without hidden harness inputs, and no hold marker may appear.

what-it-checks-in-order.name: docs-verify-release/what-it-checks-in-order-04
what-it-checks-in-order.text: Fault injection, crash recovery, race controls and independent trie-capability observations run in the explicit test build. Their unchanged assertions are separate required CI evidence. They do not claim to have run inside these extracted release binaries.

what-you-run.name: docs-verify-release/what-you-run-01
what-you-run.text: You need Nix with flakes enabled, on Linux: the verifier is built for x86_64-linux and aarch64-linux only, and it does not run on macOS. Nothing else: no checkout, no credentials, no running node.

what-you-run.name: docs-verify-release/what-you-run-02
what-you-run.text: The example names v0.12.0; the newest release is always at https://github.com/lambdasistemi/singular/releases/latest, and its tag goes in both places. Name the release you are checking twice: once to choose the verifier that release ships, once as the release to download. The verifier downloads the release's three published assets from its GitHub release page without logging in:

what-you-run.name: docs-verify-release/what-you-run-03
what-you-run.text: The archive is unpacked into a fresh temporary directory, never inside a checkout. Pass --work DIR to choose that directory and keep what it leaves behind: the downloaded assets, the extracted archive and the receipts of every command the journey ran.

acceptance-scenarios.name: specs-protocol-spec/acceptance-scenarios-01
acceptance-scenarios.text: These scenarios are specification obligations. They have not been executed as tests or proved. The branch's Markdown checks do not validate them. The last column names the sections above that govern each scenario.

acceptance-scenarios.name: specs-protocol-spec/acceptance-scenarios-02
acceptance-scenarios.text: A concrete protocol must also demonstrate conservation of representative supply and custody across every allowed transaction shape, including attempts to bypass request creation or to mint/burn outside the coupled registry transitions.

entities-and-terminology.name: specs-protocol-spec/entities-and-terminology-01
entities-and-terminology.text: A registry has an authenticated identity and a map from keys to payload-free Active or Over values. An absent key has no entry. A representative NFT identifies the active registration of a key within its registry. An Insert request UTxO carries an application-minted Insert action token; Update/Delete requests carry the existing representative. Any additional Update/Delete request-token construction remains open. A configured application policy provides the application authorization anchor, including accepted approval for Insert. The application spending script governs legal spends of the application's NFT UTxO.

entities-and-terminology.name: specs-protocol-spec/entities-and-terminology-02
entities-and-terminology.text: Registry identity, representative policy, request-token issuance, application authorization policy and application spending script are distinct semantic roles. Their actual script hashes may coincide if an implementation shares a script; this specification neither requires nor forbids that sharing.

entities-and-terminology.name: specs-protocol-spec/entities-and-terminology-03
entities-and-terminology.text: The design interface target is one application-specific parameter: the configured application policy ID. Registry identity and native policy settings are separate protocol configuration; Insert initial state and destination are approved per-request values. Sufficiency of this interface for a concrete protocol is not yet proved. The application policy mints Insert and Withdraw action tokens directly. Singular recognizes the configured policy ID and recomputes their action-bound asset names; no second mandatory native request policy/token is required for these actions.

entities-and-terminology.name: specs-protocol-spec/entities-and-terminology-04
entities-and-terminology.text: Withdraw cancels a pending Insert; it is neither registry Delete nor a staking-reward withdrawal/plugin invocation. Registry Update means retirement. An application update means an application-defined state transition and is not a registry operation.

executing-witnesses-and-net-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/executing-witnesses-and-net-minting-01
executing-witnesses-and-net-minting.text: Every native transition, supply and custody obligation MUST have an executing ledger witness. The concrete division of checks among Singular's request/registry spending validators and representative policy remains the open decision on transaction shapes and libraries; it MUST NOT rely on an unexecuted receiving validator or an assumed per-operation policy invocation.

executing-witnesses-and-net-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/executing-witnesses-and-net-minting-02
executing-witnesses-and-net-minting.text: The mint field records net quantities by asset. If a future construction reuses a representative asset identity across Delete/reinsert and combines those operations, their negative/positive quantities may cancel. The protocol MUST still enforce each logical transition and its custody effects through executing witnesses; it MUST NOT assume the representative policy necessarily runs for an empty net mint field. Fresh identities or batch restrictions are possible construction choices, not adopted requirements.

executing-witnesses-and-net-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/executing-witnesses-and-net-minting-03
executing-witnesses-and-net-minting.text: Moving an existing action token MUST NOT be treated as re-execution of its minting policy. Its certified scope, custody and disposal rules MUST account for later movement or reuse. This includes the distinction between a currently consumed request and an authorization that may intentionally permit repeated use within a specified scope.

folding-and-actor-permissions.name: specs-protocol-spec/folding-and-actor-permissions-01
folding-and-actor-permissions.text: A fold MUST apply requests against successive authenticated map states, including Insert absence and Update/Delete existing-value checks. Singular's own fold logic MUST recognize authorization and check explicit native output requirements without a mandatory arbitrary application-validation callback. This is not a guarantee that every application fits or that no application policy executes in the folding transaction. A nonzero net burn of an application action asset invokes that policy. Whether its burn branch avoids repeating costly semantic checks depends on the unresolved disposal contract; no performance improvement is established here.

folding-and-actor-permissions.name: specs-protocol-spec/folding-and-actor-permissions-02
folding-and-actor-permissions.text: Singular MUST impose no native owner, privileged requester or privileged folder gate. Anyone MAY submit a transaction satisfying the applicable protocol requirements. This does not remove application validation or establish inclusion fairness.

illustrative-naming-demo-obligations.name: specs-protocol-spec/illustrative-naming-demo-obligations-01
illustrative-naming-demo-obligations.text: These obligations derive from the proposed naming walkthrough. They make the minimal demo recognizable; they are not new Singular application-authorization or naming-schema rules. The demo is not implemented, and its application choices require the naming-profile decision before executable conformance can be assessed.

illustrative-naming-demo-obligations.name: specs-protocol-spec/illustrative-naming-demo-obligations-02
illustrative-naming-demo-obligations.text: The resolver's ledger authentication, application authorization and name normalization remain demo choices. Neither a trusted indexer nor application correctness is established merely by these stories. Liveness, inclusion fairness and race-free user ordering are not guaranteed.

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-01
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: Minting an Insert request token MUST require accepted application certification of the exact proposal. Native format validity alone MUST NOT authorize Insert. The certification MUST bind:

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-02
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: target registry, Insert operation and key;

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-03
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: configured application policy identity and evidence;

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-05
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: destination application spending script and address constraints;

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-06
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: representative identity/quantity as prescribed by registry rules and any other declared output value/effect constraints.

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-07
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: The application policy ID MUST be an authenticated Singular parameter bound to the registry's rules. A requester MUST NOT gain approval by choosing an arbitrary self-issued policy. The certification mechanism MUST prevent substitution of any bound field after approval.

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-08
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: Approval MUST be established when the Insert request token is minted; this requirement is not deferred to folding. The configured application policy MUST mint the Insert action token directly. Its asset name MUST commit to the Insert tag, registry, key, initial application datum, destination and declared required effects. Singular MUST recompute and match this name when consuming the request. Certification MUST NOT be treated as a reservation of the key or a guarantee of inclusion/order.

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-09
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: The application's minting policy MUST enforce the initial request output constraints in the creating transaction. Singular recognition authenticates the configured issuer, not the correctness of arbitrary application code. Claims about approved application semantics are conditional on the configured policy and application spending script implementing their declared contracts.

insert-approval-at-request-minting.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-approval-at-request-minting-10
insert-approval-at-request-minting.text: Declared required effects MUST be explicit native output parameters supported by the eventual schema: representative identity/quantity, destination, datum and supported value constraints. They MUST NOT imply an unspecified universal transaction-predicate language. Applications needing additional fresh observations or effects at folding are outside demonstrated precertification coverage unless the native contract explicitly supports them.

insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal-01
insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.text: A pending Insert request MUST contain no representative NFT. A representative for its requested key may already exist elsewhere: admission of an Insert request does not assert absence.

insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal-02
insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.text: Successful folding MUST check absence in the applicable successive registry state and MUST produce exactly the representative output specified by the certified proposal, including its destination and initial state. Registry insertion and representative creation MUST occur atomically in that folding transaction. The fold MUST NOT accept Insert for an occupied key.

insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal-03
insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.text: Insert requests MUST support withdrawal before successful folding. Withdrawal MUST NOT change registry state or mint a representative. Cancellation authorization MUST originate from a separate Withdraw action token minted by the configured application policy. Its asset name MUST commit to the Withdraw tag, registry, exact pending Insert UTxO and required refund terms/effects. Singular MUST check the configured policy and this exact action binding when consuming the pending Insert. An Insert action token alone MUST NOT authorize Withdraw.

insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.name: specs-protocol-spec/insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal-04
insert-pending-completion-and-withdrawal.text: The application's approval conditions, precise refund economics and token disposal remain open under the decisions on action encoding and on Withdraw economics. No representative minting or registry transition is permitted during Withdraw. The protocol MUST NOT interpret withdrawal availability as arbitrary access to deposits or arbitrary cancellation authority.

native-request-construction.name: specs-protocol-spec/native-request-construction-01
native-request-construction.text: Insert and Withdraw MUST use action tokens minted under the configured application policy. The application's minting policy MUST enforce the required approval and certified request construction when minting an action asset. The releasing application spending validator MUST enforce the exact output binding/custody when creating an Update/Delete request. Singular's spending witnesses MUST check applicable native structure, operation, binding and custody when consuming requests; for action assets, they MUST recognize the configured policy ID and recompute the expected action-bound name. Tokens issued by an arbitrary substitute policy MUST NOT be accepted. Any additional Update/Delete request token and its issuer remain a construction detail under the open decision on action encoding and token lifecycle.

native-request-construction.name: specs-protocol-spec/native-request-construction-02
native-request-construction.text: Creating an output at Singular's address MUST NOT be treated as execution of its spending validator or proof of request admission. Malformed outsider outputs may exist at the address; Singular MUST refuse to process them as valid requests. No additional creation-time native request policy is assumed.

native-request-construction.name: specs-protocol-spec/native-request-construction-03
native-request-construction.text: Action-token asset names MUST hash an unambiguous canonical encoding with domain separation between Insert and Withdraw. The specific hash function and binary schema remain open.

native-request-construction.name: specs-protocol-spec/native-request-construction-04
native-request-construction.text: The application constructs the transaction; the configured application policy ID is its authorization anchor. Request creation MUST be supportable without observing the mutable registry UTxO. This requirement does not prohibit application inputs, transaction-context checks or authenticated registry configuration.

open-decisions.name: specs-protocol-spec/open-decisions-01
open-decisions.text: Resolving these decisions, implementing the protocol, proving its properties and verifying its ledger behavior are subsequent work. No mandatory general-purpose application callback or KERI lifecycle mapping is introduced here.

purpose-and-scope.name: specs-protocol-spec/purpose-and-scope-01
purpose-and-scope.text: Singular is a permissionless registry on Cardano for unique identities and independent application state. It uses an authenticated MPF map and representative NFTs. This specification covers registry operations, native requests, certification and custody. It does not select an implementation language, a certificate encoding, a generic application plugin, a KERI integration or a shared-library API.

reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.name: specs-protocol-spec/reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guarantees-00
reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.text: Reading a registry: what each layer guarantees.

reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.name: specs-protocol-spec/reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guarantees-01
reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.text: Mallory creates a genuine registry: a real state token, minted by the real contract. Its datum pins an active policy of her own, and she mints alice under that policy with a payload she chose. Bob is handed the registry's address. A program that reads the datum and believes what it pins shows Bob Mallory's alice. A program that first derives the policies the application pins for this registry and compares them with the datum's refuses the registry before it shows anything, and says which pinned policy is not the one it derived.

reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.name: specs-protocol-spec/reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guarantees-02
reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.text: Each layer guarantees one thing, and a reader needs all three:

reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.name: specs-protocol-spec/reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guarantees-03
reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.text: Creation does not check the pins. They are chosen freely at boot, and the witness policy at minting checks only that its registry's state token is spent. A token under a registry's pinned active policy therefore means nothing until a reader has compared the pins with its own derivation.

reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.name: specs-protocol-spec/reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guarantees-04
reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.text: A reader MUST compare a registry's pinned policies with the policies it derives, and MUST do so before it shows any fact about the registry or builds any transaction for it. The three witness policies are the blueprint's witness script applied to the registry's identity, which is the state policy followed by the token name. An application that knows its own script, whether it states it as a blueprint title applied to the registry, as a compiled script or as a hash, MUST also compare the application policy. A program that cannot derive the application policy, because it is told only the registry, takes it from the datum, MUST compare the other three, and MUST say wherever it shows registry content that the application policy was not checked against any blueprint.

reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.name: specs-protocol-spec/reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guarantees-05
reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.text: The pinned policies are compared when the registry is resolved, and not again inside the same run. That is enough because every fold preserves them on chain: the state contract refuses a fold that alters one, so a later read of the state output in the same run carries the pins the comparison already accepted.

reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.name: specs-protocol-spec/reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guarantees-06
reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.text: A reader that trusts the datum instead is shown whatever the registry's creator pinned. An always-true active policy lets its creator mint a token named after any key, with any payload, and the registry's own contracts then fold it. The counts, roots and leaves such a reader prints stay consistent with the chain, because the registry is genuine; they say nothing about whether its tokens mean anything to the application.

reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.name: specs-protocol-spec/reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guarantees-07
reading-a-registry-what-each-layer-guara.text: The comparison protects the programs that run it. Another program that reads the chain MUST run the same comparison, and this page is where it learns that. Making the pins unforgeable at creation is a change to the contracts and is not part of this specification yet.

registry-transitions-and-representative-.name: specs-protocol-spec/registry-transitions-and-representative-supply-01
registry-transitions-and-representative-.text: A successful fold MUST apply only these transitions and their coupled representative effects:

registry-transitions-and-representative-.name: specs-protocol-spec/registry-transitions-and-representative-supply-02
registry-transitions-and-representative-.text: Over MUST be terminal. An Over key MUST have no live representative. Delete MUST permit a later Insert for that key, subject to approval valid for that registration and absence at that later fold. No alternative Update pair is supported.

registry-transitions-and-representative-.name: specs-protocol-spec/registry-transitions-and-representative-supply-03
registry-transitions-and-representative-.text: Active MUST denote an outstanding representative, including while that representative is in a pending request. It MUST NOT assert an application's usability or local business state. The registry values MUST contain no application payload.

replay-and-reincarnation.name: specs-protocol-spec/replay-and-reincarnation-01
replay-and-reincarnation.text: The custody rules MUST prevent two simultaneous pending Update/Delete requests from holding the same authentic representative. Consuming a request UTxO MUST prevent consuming that same UTxO again.

replay-and-reincarnation.name: specs-protocol-spec/replay-and-reincarnation-02
replay-and-reincarnation.text: Approval from a previous registration MUST NOT authorize a later incarnation outside its certified scope. If approval was limited to the previous incarnation, the later registration needs fresh approval; deliberately reusable approval is not ruled out if the application protocol selects and bounds it. A concrete scope/incarnation-binding rule is required under the open decision on incarnation scope. UTxO single-spend alone MUST NOT be presented as establishing this broader property.

singular-protocol-specification-draft.name: specs-protocol-spec/singular-protocol-specification-draft-01
singular-protocol-specification-draft.text: Status. This page records the original three-operation design: Insert, Update and Delete requests, an application-minted Withdraw, and the states Absent, Active and Over. The registry-mode model that the Lean proves, the simulator replays and the conformance suite compares against the deployed validators moves a key through seven edges and calls the terminal state Terminal; where the two differ, registry mode is current. How a name moves in the registry shows the seven edges, and the model ledger records what replaced each part of this design.

singular-protocol-specification-draft.name: specs-protocol-spec/singular-protocol-specification-draft-02
singular-protocol-specification-draft.text: This specification derives from the overview, lifecycle and certification design, with a bounded prior-art comparison and an illustrative naming walkthrough. It records required behavior, not an implemented wire protocol. MUST and MUST NOT express requirements of the intended protocol. The open decisions at the end prevent treating this as a complete implementation contract.

the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.name: specs-protocol-spec/the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development-network-00
the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.text: The forged registry, run on a development network.

the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.name: specs-protocol-spec/the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development-network-01
the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.text: A reader can watch the refusal rather than read about it. A hosted journey builds the registry of the story on a development network and runs the packaged programs against it. It is the evidence for the trust model above.

the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.name: specs-protocol-spec/the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development-network-02
the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.text: A test harness boots the registry. It is not a product command, because no command a user runs can pin a policy the release does not derive. The harness uses the real boot and the real contracts, and the datum it writes pins an always-true script as the active policy. It then mints a token named alice under that policy. The development network's own record of the chain shows a reader that trusts the datum exactly what the story says: a token named alice, under the policy the datum pins, held by the wallet.

the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.name: specs-protocol-spec/the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development-network-03
the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.text: Two more observations are recorded and not asserted. The first is evidence for hardening creation. On the forged registry, a fold that mints the token its request owes under the pinned policy and, beside it, a token under the honest witness policy was accepted by the node. The honest witness policy accepts any mint while its registry's state is spent in a fold, and the state contract checks the mint only under the three pinned policies, so on a forged registry the honest witness policy is not pinned and a fold can mint under it freely. A fold that mints under the honest active policy instead of the pinned one is refused by the state script.

the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.name: specs-protocol-spec/the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development-network-04
the-forged-registry-run-on-a-development.text: The second is the check that makes one comparison per command enough. A fold that swaps the active policy in the new state datum for the always-true script is refused by the node, which names the state script as the script that failed it, and the same fold without the swap is accepted. The deployed scripts carry no trace, so the node's answer names the failing script and not the check. The contract's own tests of that alteration name the check pins-altered.

update-and-delete-application-authorizat.name: specs-protocol-spec/update-and-delete-application-authorization-01
update-and-delete-application-authorizat.text: An Update/Delete request MUST carry the existing authentic representative for its exact registry/key, at the Singular request address. An additional request token, if any, is a construction detail under the open decision on action encoding and token lifecycle.

update-and-delete-application-authorizat.name: specs-protocol-spec/update-and-delete-application-authorization-02
update-and-delete-application-authorizat.text: The application spending validator MUST authorize transfer from application custody into that exact request, including operation, registry/key and destination. The application remains responsible for the legality of the release under its own rules. Mere NFT spendability MUST NOT be treated as blanket authorization of any registry operation.

update-and-delete-application-authorizat.name: specs-protocol-spec/update-and-delete-application-authorization-03
update-and-delete-application-authorizat.text: The application spending validator MUST enforce the request format, exact binding and custody in the release transaction. Singular MUST check the native conditions when consuming the request. Neither transfer to the address nor movement of an existing token alone invokes a receiving or minting policy. No second application attestation token is required solely to repeat a valid operation-specific release authorization. The application MUST NOT be able to bypass Singular's representative supply or request custody requirements.

update-and-delete-custody-and-completion.name: specs-protocol-spec/update-and-delete-custody-and-completion-00
update-and-delete-custody-and-completion.text: Update and Delete custody and completion.

update-and-delete-custody-and-completion.name: specs-protocol-spec/update-and-delete-custody-and-completion-01
update-and-delete-custody-and-completion.text: Pending Update/Delete requests MUST retain their representative until valid completion. They MUST NOT support ordinary withdrawal, rejection or sweep that releases it.

update-and-delete-custody-and-completion.name: specs-protocol-spec/update-and-delete-custody-and-completion-02
update-and-delete-custody-and-completion.text: Valid completion MUST consume the request, burn its representative and apply its specified registry transition atomically. A pending representative MUST NOT also remain available for independent application rotation. A completed request MUST NOT be accepted again; the concrete request-token lifecycle must satisfy this requirement.
